“Super Intelligence and new ways of organizing research are opening entirely new frontiers of discovery,” reads the statement, which was seen by NBC News. “We recognize the opportunity to take advantage of these changes.”

Michael Kratsios, head of the White House’s Office of Science and Technology Policy, spearheaded the vision statement, which also says the participating countries welcome the “growing field of metascience,” a term that describes the study of the scientific process itself.
Tech ministers from Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates were among the representatives from other countries that endorsed the statement.

In remarks Kratsios plans to deliver at the forum, shared in advance with NBC News, he will outline a vision for an era of scientific progress in which laboratories run by robots and AI systems can design scientific experiments, iterate and analyze results at superhuman speeds.
“Super intelligence applied to science will be an incredible force for democratization of research and breakthrough developments,” he plans to say.

Leading AI companies Anthropic and OpenAI have recently launched initiatives to connect biomedical laboratories to powerful AI systems, while other companies have attempted to automate laboratories for years.

“The landscape has changed everywhere, the ground is moving beneath our feet, and we must all reinvigorate our research enterprise and lay new foundations for knowledge, innovation and prosperity,” Kratsios is expected to say in his remarks.
The vision statement also says that public trust is the bedrock of scientific innovation and progress and that there’s value in “a deliberate portfolio of funding mechanisms” for science.

The Trump administration has repeatedly attempted to make drastic cuts to federal funding for scientific research. Its proposed budget for the 2027 fiscal year would, for example, cut funding for the National Science Foundation by about half.

Gretchen Goldman, president and CEO of the Union of Concerned Scientists, said the administration had undermined many scientific research efforts. “They’ve shattered the trust of the American people in the way they’ve treated the U.S. science and technology enterprise,” she said, pointing in particular to cuts to the National Institutes of Health.
“It’s hard to take seriously any promises of increased trust and transparency when you look at the actions they’ve taken,” Goldman said.

The statement comes as part of a wider push by Kratsios to reform how the U.S. incentivizes scientific innovation. In July, he submitted a report to Trump recommending changes to the ways the federal government funds research. He plans to host a summit about it in Washington, D.C., on Thursday with scientific and business leaders.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Kratsios is also leading the Genesis Mission, a national effort Trump launched last year to “unleash a new age of AI‑accelerated innovation and discovery.”
The forthcoming vision statement puts a particular emphasis on metascience, an area of study that has received wider government attention in recent years.

Its prominence in the statement signals increased international adoption, according to Jenn Gustetic, director of metascience and research and development policy at the nonpartisan think tank Institute for Progress.
“Metascience efforts have built momentum in the U.K. and the U.S. and it’s encouraging to see other nations embrace this mindset of experimentation and evidence building,” Gustetic said.

In September, the National Science Foundation announced that it would establish an Office of Metascience (OMS), charged with evaluating new approaches to funding and identifying which award mechanisms lead to the best scientific outcomes.

“Through the OMS, NSF will become a learning, self-improving institution that tries new approaches, measures their effects, admits candidly when they do not work, and scales them when they succeed,” the agency’s acting director Brian Stone wrote in a letter.
The Science and Technology in Society Forum is intended as a venue for leaders to discuss how to maximize the benefits of science and address ethical and safety issues.

During the three-day gathering, scientists and policymakers from around the world are expected to discuss how AI is impacting education, how experts can foster trust in scientific research, recent breakthroughs in personalized medicine and more.

The vision statement is set to be released just days after Trump gathered the country’s leading tech executives at the White House to forge consensus on how to regulate and minimize risks from AI. The meeting culminated in the “White House Accord on Super Intelligence,” which laid out a four-part voluntary approach for companies to independently oversee their own safety protocols.
Kratsios participated in the AI meeting.

“If you take the risks and benefits of superintelligence seriously, the most important thing you can do is to develop your country’s ability to understand and use it,” he said at a United Nations Security Council meeting on AI last month.

title: Search continues for 6 on board medical evacuation jet after debris field found off Nantucket
summary: The U.S. Coast Guard has located a debris field off the coast of Nantucket from an air ambulance flight that lost contact with air traffic controllers Saturday morning, it said.
story: The U.S. Coast Guard has located a debris field off the coast of Nantucket from an air ambulance flight that lost contact with air traffic controllers Saturday morning, it said.
The search will continue throughout the night for the six people who were on board the aircraft, the Coast Guard said. Four Canadian nationals and two Bermudian nationals were on the plane, it said.
The Gulfstream G100 jet was en route to Boston from the island of Bermuda, the Coast Guard said earlier Saturday.
Air and surface crews were searching an area off the coast of Nantucket after it was informed at 2 a.m. that a jet had lost contact with air traffic controllers.
The plane was carrying out a medical evacuation in Bermuda, said Clarence Togeretz, the director of flight operations at Latitude Air Ambulance, which operates the plane.

Latitude Air Ambulance operates specially equipped private planes to transport and treat sick or injured people. It serves private clients, patients who required advanced care and insured patients who become critically ill or injured while abroad, according to the medical transportation company’s website.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement that it issued a search-and-rescue notice for the jet at 1:20 a.m. ET Saturday.
Air traffic control tower audio from Boston, obtained by NBC News, appears to indicate that controllers asked the aircraft if it was “coming in blind.”
Controllers later ask another plane to “attempt contact” with the jet. It is unclear whether that attempt was successful.

Emergency services audio obtained by NBC News asked vessels to keep a “sharp lookout” for any signs of a “possible aircraft in the water.” Data from Flightradar24 showed a number of aircraft searching south of the island.
A spokesperson for the Massachusetts Port Authority, which operates Boston Logan International Airport, said: “Our thoughts are with those on board and their loved ones as the search continues.”
Bermuda is a British overseas territory in the North Atlantic, about 650 miles from North Carolina.
Bermuda Premier David Burt said in a statement that his “thoughts are with everyone on board and their families during this deeply worrying time.”

title: Flydubai pilot attacked captain with cockpit’s crash ax in attempted terrorist act, UAE official says
summary: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.
story: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.

The suspect is Omani citizen Hamam al-Hammami, multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East told NBC News. Authorities have not officially released the identity.
The Wall Street Journal, citing sources familiar with the matter, reported that al-Hammami had “previously been banned from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views.”
Oman Air did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether he previously worked for the company.

Emirati officials are leading investigations into the midair incident, which occurred Wednesday on a flight carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A crash was averted, according to eyewitnesses and Israeli officials, when crew and passengers were able to enter the cabin and subdue the attacker.

“Investigations into the incident aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073 revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act,” UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said in an update on Saturday.
“The co-pilot began executing his plan during the flight, attacking the captain inside the flight deck using a crash axe and attempting to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls,” he said.
Al-Hammami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to Abu Dhabi on Thursday, the Saudi Interior Ministry said. The statement said his health had “improved,” but his medical condition was unclear.
Al Shamsi said investigations were ongoing to “establish the full circumstances, motives, and any links related to the incident.”

Israeli government spokesman David Mencer said Friday that Israeli investigators would “join their Emirati counterparts in investigating this attempted mass murder and establishing precisely what happened, his motives and background.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday: “As time passes, the picture becomes clearer: The attacker had undergone Islamist radicalization. He came to crash the plane, along with its passengers.”
He did not say how he reached that conclusion, but added: “We are investigating whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price.”
Netanyahu’s spokesman Doron Spielman told NBC News that the suspect “talks on his social media about killing Jews.”
The flight captain, Indian national Capt. Smit Machchhar, spoke for the first time Friday from a hospital in Abu Dhabi.
Flydubai pilot speaks out follow mid-air attack
Machchhar was widely praised for his efforts to prevent the plane from crashing by opening the cockpit door and allowing passengers and crew members to rush in.
Speaking from his hospital bed, Machchhar said he had been “severely injured” and “could sense that the aircraft was going down.”

“I was acting for my own life, but at the same time, I knew I couldn’t let all of them die,” he said on a video call released by India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, adding that he told himself to “give just one last push” to the cockpit door.
The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi called Machchhar the “Indian braveheart,” saying in an X post Saturday that he “remains under excellent medical care & is recovering well.”

The deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, Hamdan bin Mohammed, posted photos on X after visiting Machchhar in the hospital in which he’s seen kissing the pilot’s head and shaking his hand. Machchhar, with one arm in a cast and medical dressings on his head, appears awake and smiling.
“From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise,” he wrote.
Ayelet Epstein, a 47-year-old Israeli, told NBC News that her 14-year-old daughter asked if they were going to die when they heard shouting and “a huge fall started.”
“I told her, no, I don’t think so, we’re going to be OK,” she said, adding that “I was trying to rationalize things in a hopeful way for her.”
Epstein thanked Machchhar “from the bottom of my heart” for saving their lives, lauding his bravery.

A Flydubai spokesperson said Saturday: “We recognise that there are many questions at this stage; however, the circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation. We are therefore not in a position to comment further beyond our published statements.”
“We remain fully committed to supporting the ongoing investigation and are in close coordination with the relevant government authorities and regulators,” the spokesperson added.
President Donald Trump told reporters Thursday that there would be renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack.
“You just ask them,” he said. “They know what happened. They’ll be hit very hard.”
There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News.
Raf Sanchez and Shira Pinson reported from Tel Aviv. Freddie Clayton reported from London. Tom Winter and Jonathan Dienst reported from New York.

title: Watch Anne Hathaway ‘Disappear’ After Promoting A Marathon Of 5 Movies This Year
summary: After a year of promoting a whopping five major films, Anne Hathaway made good on her promise to get out of the spotlight.
story: After a year of promoting a whopping five major films, Anne Hathaway made good on her promise to get out of the spotlight.

The actor shared a video on her Instagram Oct. 2 —the release day of her latest film “Verity” — in which she hilariously disappears into thin air. It comes after the actor told Entertainment Tonight in a Sept. 21 clip that she had been planning to “to vanish in a plume of smoke” after her press tours were over.
Hathaway, who’s also pregnant with her third child, sure has a sense of humor.
In the clip, Hathaway speaks to the camera, telling fans that she’s “heading out to the ‘Verity’ premiere.”
“‘Verity’ comes out in theaters Friday, Oct. 2, and then on Oct. 3...,” Hathaway says before abruptly vanishing from the screen as a puff of animated smoke dissipates in the room.
The video then features a flurry of faux news stories.
“Anne Hathaway simply evaporates,” one headline says.
The clip concludes with some words from the actor, thanking her fans.
“Thank you everyone for your support, and for making this an incredible, unforgettable year,” the text says.
Now that’s how you end a press circuit.
The hilarious post comes after Hathaway not only promoted “Verity,” but also did press for “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” “Mother Mary,” “The Odyssey” and “The End of Oak Street.”
Her ubiquity in film this year led satirical outlet The Onion to release a now-viral article in August titled, “Analysts Warn U.S. Economy Becoming Overly Dependent On Anne Hathaway.”
In addition to the nonstop press tours, Hathaway is also pregnant, expecting her third child with husband Adam Schulman. The two share sons Jonathan, 10, and Jack, 6.
The actor said during her Sept. 30 appearance on “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon,” that she got the news that she was expecting just before she was set to promote one of her films.

“I found out I was pregnant like, two-and-a-half weeks before ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’ press tour kicked off,” said Hathaway, who announced her pregnancy in June. “And I was just like, ‘How is that gonna work?’”
While it’s been quite the amount of work, Hathaway told the Associated Press that it’s not necessary to “over praise the pampered actress.”

“There’s a lot of pregnant women out there at home and in the workplace who didn’t get a manicure this morning,” she told the outlet in a Sept. 29 interview. “I’m very happy to do my job. I have so much support.”

title: Dennis Miller’s Fellow ‘Monday Night Football’ Announcer Fondly Recalls the ‘Experiment’ to Add Him to the Booth
summary: Dan Fouts recalls being on “Monday Night Football” with Dennis Miller for their two-season run on the broadcast.
story: It was an audacious move.

In an effort to jumpstart interest in “Monday Night Football,” ABC hired Dennis Miller to serve as part of the broadcast team in the booth in 2000, joining play-by-play legend Al Michaels and Pro Football Hall of Famer Dan Fouts, who served as color analyst.

It was a move met with cheers and jeers at the time. Don Ohlmeyer, who had produced “MNF” during its glory days with Howard Cosell, Frank Gifford and Don Meredith, returned to the broadcast tasked with injecting life into the program. He thought way outside the tackle box by bringing in Miller, a comedian known for arcane references and a run on “Saturday Night Live,” where he anchored “Weekend Update” from 1985 until 1991.
Miller’s stint on “MNF” is the subject of a new NFL Shorts documentary that premiered Sept. 29 on HBO called “Miller Night Football.”
The decision to hire him on “MNF” didn’t only catch the public off-guard, though.
“It was an honest reaction of ‘What?!,’ but I was a fan of Dennis,” Fouts, who is featured in the HBO documentary, tells TODAY.com.

“I was excited to meet him, but then figured out that this was kind of an experiment of Don Ohlmeyer’s to try to put something unique on the air for Monday night, kind of like the old days when they had Howard Cosell in the booth,” he says. “I think the idea was to have something that was a little controversial. So I was all onboard for it because it was ‘Monday Night Football.’”

Miller wasn’t a total neophyte in the broadcasting game. By the time he was hired, he had already won five Emmy Awards for his HBO series “Dennis Miller Live.” And while athletes had previously crossed over into the world of pop culture and news — TODAY’s Joe Garagiola, a former baseball player, was an early pioneer when he joined the show in 1967 — a comedian sliding into the booth on one of America’s most hallowed sports programs was unprecedented.
While headlines followed the hiring, Miller was not content to go for laughs just for the sake of getting them.

“I thought that Dennis came well prepared each week. He was excited about the job,” says Fouts, who started his run on “MNF” the same year Miller did and previously played quarterback for the San Diego Chargers between 1973 and 1987, making six Pro Bowls.

Panned by some, lauded by others, Miller’s presence in the booth provided renewed interest in “MNF,” as he had quips at the ready, oftentimes prepping them in advance, with Michael, Fouts and sideline reporter Melissa Stark.

“In Dennis’ mind, you know, he had things that he wanted to say, and he put him in there in his style, and it took awhile to figure out what the rhythm was,” Fouts says. “But once we got going … we got used to each other, and of course, having Al Michaels in the booth was the key because he’s the conductor of that train.”

As the documentary details, things changed in the second season, in 2001. Ohlmeyer left “MNF.” The Sept. 11 terror attacks put a pause on America’s appetite for laughter, several games were noncompetitive and Miller had studied the game to get more into Xs and Os. And then came the big development after the season ended: John Madden, considered the best analyst in the sport, was a free agent, with his contract at Fox running out. ABC came calling.
“He was available, and you just don’t turn down that opportunity to have the Babe Ruth of sports broadcasting,” Fouts says.
Without the confluence of events that preceded Miller and Fouts’ departure from “MNF,” could they and Michaels have continued?
“Oh, definitely,” Fouts says.

Fouts says he and Miller speak “once in a while” and “shared a few laughs” while talking to each other about the documentary. As he reflects a quarter of a century after his time with Miller and Michaels ended, he feels pride in playing a role in once again making “MNF” a water cooler show.
“Looking back at it, I think the documentary tells you that it was entertaining,” he said. “The goal was to bring the interest of ‘Monday Night Football’ back, and I certainly think it did that.”

title: Lindsay Lohan Recreates ‘Mean Girls’ Scene For A Most Fetch October 3rd
summary: Lindsay Lohan, who played main character Cady Heron in “Mean Girls,” shared a video on social media, recreating the fan favorite scene in which Cady has an interaction with her school crush Aaron Samuels.
story: Attention all Plastics, Art Freaks, Preps and more — Lindsay Lohan is here to remind us that today’s the day.

The “Mean Girls” star, who played main character Cady Heron in the 2004 comedy, shared a video on social media, recreating the fan favorite scene in which Cady has an interaction with her school crush Aaron Samuels.
Though Jonathan Bennett, who played Aaron, isn’t featured in the clip, the video still sends us back to the early aughts.
The video shows Lohan sitting at a school desk behind another individual.
“On October 3rd, he asked me what day it was,” Lohan says in a voiceover that’s since become an internet classic.
“It’s October 3rd,” Lohan says in the clip just as she did in the film, before winking at the camera. Of course, it was posted on Oct. 3.

For years, the scene has been a source of internet fodder, with fans recreating it annually. It’s popularity has also given rise to what’s now known as “Mean Girls Day.” Lohan herself has observed the cult holiday in the past, posting stills from the famous scene on Oct. 3.
Comedian Tim Meadows, who played Principal Duvall in the comedy, released a skit just ahead of the holiday on social media in the form of a fake personal injury attorney ad.

“Sometimes it’s not easy to admit when you need help,” Meadows says in the skit, shared on Oct. 2. “It happened to me 20 years ago, but it feels like it was just yesterday. Every October 3rd is a reminder of her. Regina George.”
Attorney Mike Morse than asks the iconic question from the film, “Have you or anyone you know, ever felt personally victimized by Regina George?”
Regardless of whether Regina George ever punched you in the face (and it was awesome), here are some “Mean Girls” Day celebrations ideas.

title: Sarah Jessica Parker and Matthew Broderick’s Latest Date Night Looks Are Just Too Darling
summary: Celebrity couple Sarah Jessica Parker and Matthew Broderick attended the NYC Ballet Fall Fashion Gala at Lincoln Center together in Manhattan on Oct. 1.
story: This must be what that can’t-live-without-each-other love looks like!
Celebrity couple Sarah Jessica Parker and Matthew Broderick attended the NYC Ballet Fall Fashion Gala at Lincoln Center together in Manhattan on Oct. 1.
And just like that, the longtime married couple took fans’ breaths away with their stunning looks.

The “Sex and the City” star sported a sheer, pink tulle Simone Rocha dress that featured long, baby pink ribbons and floral accents. Her hair was styled in a long, voluminous braid down her back. A few ribbons were also incorporated into the dramatic braid.
Parker tied the outfit together with a bag that matched the shade of her dress, along with a pair glittering pointed-toe stilletos.
Broderick brought his own shine as he sported a classic black tux that was accented by a white flower lapel.

Parker, who has been married to Broderick since 1997, is the founding chair of the event, which was first established in 2012. It serves as an annual fundraiser for the NYC Ballet. Others big name attendees included legendary musician Stevie Nicks, the evening’s honorary chair and model Julia Fox, who served as a gala chair.
Fans, of course, had no chill over the stunning looks.
Several people on social media dubbed Parker “Rapunzel” for her long locks while others commented about the couple’s sweet poses as the two held hands amid several photos.
Parker and Broderick have three children together: son James Wilkie Broderick, born in October 2002, and twin daughters Tabitha Hodge Broderick and Marion Loretta Elwell Broderick, born in June 2009.
Parker, who met Broderick in 1991, told the New York Times that it was actually her brothers who had introduced her to her now-husband.
Broderick told “Watch What Happens Live” in 2022 that it didn’t take long for him to know that she was “the one.”
“Oh, the first time I met her,” Broderick told host Andy Cohen. “I saw her walking down the street and thought, ‘That’s it.’”

title: Ken Urker, Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s Boyfriend and Father of Her Daughter, Has Died
summary: More details have emerged after Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner and father of her daughter was found dead by police on Oct. 1 at a home in Louisiana.
story: More details have emerged after Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner and father of her daughter was found dead by police on Oct. 1 at a home in Louisiana.
The Lafourche Parish Sherriff’s Office issued an initial statement to NBC News Oct. 1 confirming that Ken Urker was found dead by deputies at a residence in Raceland, Louisiana. He was 34.

A preliminary report obtained by NBC News from the Lafourche Parish Sherriff’s Office on Oct. 2 calls the incident “drug related,” and the incident code is listed as “overdose.” Police said they found no signs of foul play.

According to the report, Blanchard’s half brother, Dylan Blanchard, and another person, Justin Daigle, told police they gained access to Urker’s unlocked bedroom window and entered the home after seeing Urker unconscious on his bed. Daigle told police Urker was “not breathing.”

Authorities were initially called by Anita Blanchard, who said that she and the two other men were trying to get access to Urker’s home because he had not been answering his phone or his front door, per the report.

Anita Blanchard, Dylan Blanchard and Daigle told the deputies when they arrived at the residence that Urker was dead, according to the report. Deputies entered the home and found syringes and a spoon in the bathroom next to “a brown powdery substance,” according to the report. They also located a syringe and a handgun on the nightstand next to the bed.
Urker had a paper towel placed on his left arm “with what appeared to be blotches of blood” on it, per the report.
Anita Blanchard and Dylan Blanchard told police Urker had made comments to them about being “depressed and upset” while with them at church on Sept. 30, according to the report.
Lafourche Parish Coroner Kayla Breaux said in a statement to NBC News that an autopsy was conducted Oct. 2 and “there is no definitive cause of death” at this time.

“The case remains pending completion of toxicology testing, and no further information regarding the cause of death will be available until those results are received and the investigation is complete,” Breaux said in the statement.

Gypsy Rose Blanchard told People magazine in an interview published Oct. 2 that Urker died of an overdose. TODAY has reached out to Blanchard as well as A+E Global Media, which owns Lifetime, the network that airs Blanchard’s reality show, “Gypsy Rose: Life After Lockup,” but did not immediately receive responses.

Blanchard and Urker first met when Blanchard was still in prison for her role in her allegedly abusive mother’s 2015 murder. The two got engaged in 2018 before they broke it off a year later. Blanchard was released from prison in 2023 after serving more than eight years of her 10-year sentence.
She and Urker eventually rekindled in 2024 and welcomed a daughter. In speaking to People on Oct. 2, Blanchard called Urker her soulmate.
“Ken was an amazing father and a man who was deeply loved,” she said. “He will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase.”
In the time that she and Urker broke up, Blanchard married another man, Ryan Scott Anderson, in 2022. They separated in 2024 and finalized their divorce in December of that year.

Blanchard and Urker reconnected and announced in July 2024 that they were expecting a child together. They welcomed a baby girl, Aurora, on Dec. 28, 2024, just weeks after she finalized her divorce from Anderson.

“We honestly didn’t have a plan,” Blanchard told TODAY.com in March 2025. “It was really one of those things that we’re winging. So, whenever it comes to the scrutiny, we just hold true to each other. We lean on each other for support. One has to be the strong one, and then the other has a moment of rest and weakness to just let all of that sink in.”

Urker first connected with Blanchard in 2017, when he wrote a letter to her while she was an inmate at a Missouri state prison. He had learned about her story from watching “Mommy Dead and Dearest,” a 2017 HBO documentary about the murder of Blanchard’s mother, Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard, as well as the abuse Blanchard suffered throughout her childhood.

Blanchard is thought to be a victim of Munchausen syndrome by proxy, a psychological disorder where a “caregiver feigns, exaggerates or induces illness in (another person) with the primary goal being to get attention, sympathy and praise,” Dr. Marc Feldman, a board-certified psychiatrist, said in a previous interview with TODAY.com.
Nicholas Godejohn, Blanchard’s ex-boyfriend who carried out the murder of her mother, is serving a life sentence without the possibility of parole after first pleading not guilty.
Blanchard was still in prison when Urker proposed to her in 2018. In August 2019, they broke it off.

“There were many adults in his life, presumably much ‘wiser’ than he, who suggested it wasn’t the right time for me to be married,” Blanchard explained in her 2024 memoir, “My Time to Stand.” “‘If you love her, you’ll set her free,’ was the common piece of advice he’d hear again and again, sometimes from prominent Hollywood therapists and other media personalities — sometimes from those in my own immediate family. I see now, he believed he was acting in my best interest by sacrificing his own needs and wants.”
Urker shared on Instagram in 2024 that the couple had gotten back together after Blanchard had separated from Anderson in 2022. The two then welcomed their daughter together later that year.

“My marriage with Ryan taught me a lot about myself,” Blanchard told TODAY.com. “There was something Ryan said in Season 1 (of ‘Gypsy Rose: Life After Lock Up’), ‘Life is not a fairy tale. It’s going to have its challenges.’ I didn’t understand that at the time. Now, after going through everything, I apply that to my relationship with Ken. We will have bad days, moments where we feel overwhelmed, but to not give up. Don’t just judge the whole relationship on that one day or that one argument.”

title: Tom Cruise’s ‘Digger’ Is Dividing Critics. Read What They Are Saying
summary: Here’s a spoiler-free look at what critics are saying about “Digger” after the film received a 52% on Rotten Tomatoes.
story: Can “Digger” dig itself out of the hole the film is seemingly in after receiving mixed reviews?

Although director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s satirical black comedy starring Tom Cruise as the titular character doesn’t hit theaters until Oct. 2, it is already generating divisive conversations. Reviews for the movie started rolling in on Sept. 29 and have been split, with “Digger” landing a 52% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes as of Oct. 1.
Some are praising Cruise, who wears heavy prosthetics and sports a gray receding hairline, for delivering “an acting masterless.” Others are calling it a “languid, self-satisfied film.”

“Digger” is centered on a wealthy oil tycoon named Digger whose company is drilling off the coast of Greenland. One day, Digger receives a call from a scientist on site informing him that the drilling has caused a 5-foot crack to form in the ice, potentially leading to an environmental disaster.

“Digger here got us into this mess and Digger’s gonna dig us out again!” says John Goodman, who portrays the President of the United States. The movie also stars Riz Ahmed, Sandra Hüller, Jesse Plemons and Emma D’Arcy.

The movie’s social media pages have been leaning into the polarizing responses. The “Digger” Instagram page released a new ad that includes varying quotes from critics. “Same film different truths,” text over the clip reads.
“Decide for yourself,” the caption encouraged fans.
While we wait to see how fans react, here’s a spoiler-free look at what critics are saying about “Digger.”
The Hollywood Reporter
The first line of David Rooney’s “Digger” review made it clear he was not a fan of Iñárritu’s or Cruise’s choices in the film.

“At last, a climate crisis satire so smug and bombastic it makes Adam McKay’s ‘Don’t Look Up’ seem almost innocuous. ‘Digger’ is basically what happens when you put two outsize egos together with nobody holding the reins to keep their most self-indulgent impulses in check,” he wrote in his review for The Hollywood Reporter.

“Piloted by a spectacularly obnoxious Tom Cruise, who evidently spent hours in the makeup chair each day to look his age, Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s wannabe Dr. Strangelove is a heavy-handed cataclysm scenario built around the blunt point that any attempt to halt global warming this late in the game is pure political theater.”
He said that while the movie clearly intended to have humorous moments, it failed to nail the punchlines.

“(Iñárritu’s) eighth feature is so meta that you watch in excruciating weariness as it disappears up its own ass and then realize to your dismay that there’s another eardrum-shattering hour left to endure,” he added, not pulling any punches.
He then compared the movie to recent panned films like “Babylon,” “Amsterdam” and “Megalopolis.”
One of his only compliments was for Ahmed’s performance of scientist Ganesh. He also highlighted the movie’s parliament scene.
Variety
Variety’s Owen Gleiberman compared Cruise’s transformation in “Digger” to his character in “Tropic Thunder.”

“The performance is very much of a piece with what Cruise did in his fat-suit cameo as the vulgarian studio executive Les Grossman in ‘Tropic Thunder.’ At one point, Cruise wanted to make a Les Grossman movie, and in a certain way ‘Digger’ is that movie — a chance for him to let it rip for two hours, to give the kind of stylized hambone performance that’s essentially a ‘Saturday Night Live’ caricature, only executed with Method fullness,” he wrote.
Like other critics, he referenced Stanley Kubrick’s “Dr. Strangelove.”

“‘Digger,’ with its countdown-to-Armageddon scenario, wants to be the ‘Dr. Strangelove’ of climate change. It also wants to be the ‘Network’ of climate change, and to radically up the ante on ‘Don’t Look Up,’ Adam McKay’s finger-pointing satire of climate change,” Gleiberman said. “Did I mention that the movie is about climate change? I take that issue seriously, but at this point a movie like ‘Digger’ is practically guilt-tripping its audience.”
He also had an issue with the humor, or lack thereof.

“But here’s the real problem: ‘Digger’ isn’t funny. It’s nervy, in your face, adventurous, and bizarro in a free-swinging, out-of-the-box way. And it feels like a comedy, since it’s fueled by the relentless overacting of a bad Coen brothers movie. But ‘Dr. Strangelove,’ built around the genius of Peter Sellers, was brilliantly funny. ‘Digger’ borrows the doomsday architecture of ‘Strangelove’ but leaves out the slyness, replacing it with a lavishly overscaled spectacle of browbeating,” he said.
Vulture
Rotten Tomatoes has Bilge Ebiri’s review for Vulture labeled fresh, but his piece skews more mixed.

He praised Cruise’s commitment to the role, writing, “His caricature of a face, encrusted with prosthetic wrinkles and loose strands of thinning hair, is one thing, but the physicality is what really impresses, almost as though he’s still doing one of those ‘Mission: Impossible’ stunts. Transforming his inner imperturbability into breathless forward motion, ‘Digger’ moves with hunched, waddling determination — part George W. Bush, part Yosemite Sam, all wombat. We can’t take our eyes off him, but we never forget this is Tom Cruise doing a part.”
However, he said other aspects, like the sets and sound design, made it seem like the movie was “designed to aggravate.”

“It’s like being trapped inside a tuba for two hours — and I don’t just mean the overinsistent score by Cosmo Sheldrake. Everything is an underline, every line a shout, every glance a grimace. It’s all expectoration, no breath,” Ebiri explained.
Roger Ebert
Robert Daniels gave “Digger” two out of four stars for his Roger Ebert review.
He said the movie comes across as an amalgamation of Iñárritu’s films “Birdman” and “Bardo, False Chronicle of a Handful of Truths.”
“‘Digger’ combines both heady films, and it’s excruciatingly painful that this languid, self-satisfied film doesn’t work,” Daniels wrote. “‘Digger’ never fully commits to its high concept.”
He felt that the movie lacked substance.
BBC
BBC’s Nicholas Barber had a much more favorable opinion. He gave “Digger” four out of five stars while applauding Cruise’s risky decision to take the role.

“’Digger’ isn’t just the weirdest film Cruise has ever made, it’s the weirdest film that almost anyone has ever made,” he said. “Most people won’t go to see it — and some people who do will walk out halfway through. But that doesn’t mean that ‘Digger’ is a failure. It’s just that it’s a bizarre, hectoring, conceptually challenging eco-satire, so it’s not likely to be mistaken for ‘Mission: Impossible.’”
He teased that “Digger” features some surprising twists.

“Judged purely a satire, then, ‘Digger’ is powerfully resonant. But there is more to it than that. The film has two high-concept twists which raise new questions about everything you’ve seen so far,” Barber said.
He sums up his overall feelings about “Digger” in one sentence: “Personally, I loved it.”

He continues, “Some of its excesses are, well, a bit too excessive, and most viewers will wish it was shorter. After about 90 minutes, you get tired of close-ups of Goodman yelling while snake-sized veins bulge out of his forehead. But when Cruise is clambering all over the set, delivering thunderous lectures on the oil industry, I couldn’t help grinning at the gargantuan scale of his performance, the conviction of the script’s grim environmental message, and Iñárritu’s antic style.”
USA Today
Brian Truitt was also intrigued by Cruise signing on for this film at this point in his career.

“Wearing facial prosthetics, a faux beer belly and a Texas-sized twang, Cruise pushes his own considerable boundaries and reminds that the dude can still put on an acting masterclass when he wants,” he said in his review for USA Today. “Surrounded by a knockout supporting cast, Cruise is the best thing about Iñárritu’s latest effort, a socially conscious cautionary tale that can’t quite nail all of its lofty ambitions.”

He argues that the first twist in “Digger” “changes the film’s entire perspective while also deepening its themes. The shift is jarring when it happens but mostly works, plus doles out provocative thoughts to chew on as the credits roll.”
The Associated Press
Jake Coyle said in his review that the satire works despite “Digger” not being humorous.

“The biggest ding against ‘Digger’ is that, for a satire, it’s not particularly funny. Cruise is no Peter Sellers and Iñárritu is not Stanley Kubrick. Their strenuous efforts to reach a similar black-comedy pitch can fall flat,” he said in his review for the Associated Press.
However, he appreciated how timely the film is and that it stands out among current releases.

“But ‘Digger’ is sharper on the other side of tragicomedy. An impassioned provocation aimed at both politicians and audience members, ‘Digger’ is by any measure an uncommon major studio release — as urgent as ‘An Inconvenient Truth’ but a whole lot more operatic. For better or worse, this is an of-the-moment big swing that’s unlikely to come along again anytime soon,” Coyle continues.
Los Angeles Times
Amy Nicholson noted at the beginning of her review for the Los Angeles Times that “Digger” marks the first time in years that Cruise has ventured outside of his comfort zone.
“After a decade of playing it safe with “Mission: Impossible” and “Top Gun” sequels, this is what it looks like when Hollywood’s last classic movie star finally sticks out his neck,” she said.
Nicholson wasn’t completely sold on the film, but she is pleased it was made.

She explained, “There are no emotions in it, only our own cold and cruel fears reflected back at us, as with a shot of Cruise standing defiantly in front of a mirror rimmed by antlers. It’s about inertia and abdication, not solutions, and while I don’t entirely love this strange comedy, I’m giddy that it’s lurched into existence.”

title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard and Ken Urker’s Relationship Timeline
summary: Who was Gypsy Rose Blanchard's late partner, Ken Urker? Were they married? Why did they break up? What is their daughter's name?
story: Ken Urker, the ex-fiancé of Gypsy Rose Blanchard and father of her daughter, was found dead by police on Oct. 1 at a home in Louisiana. He was 34.
“We responded to a residence at 107 Double H Drive, Lot 4, in Raceland today after receiving a call at 6:15 p.m.,” the Lafource Parish Sherriff’s Office said in a statement to NBC News.
“Kenan Urker, 34, was found dead upon arrival. At this time, we are continuing the death investigation.”
It’s the latest twist in the relationship between Blanchard and Urker, who had navigated a rocky road over the course of their romance.

The pair met when Blanchard was still behind bars for her role in her allegedly abusive mother’s 2015 murder. Since then, they had gotten engaged, called it off, got back together and started a family. Blanchard was also married to another man in between those events.

“We honestly didn’t have a plan,” she told TODAY.com in 2025 about rekindling her relationship with Urker. “It was really one of those things that we’re winging. So, whenever it comes to the scrutiny, we just hold true to each other. We lean on each other for support. One has to be the strong one, and then the other has a moment of rest and weakness to just let all of that sink in.”

Blanchard is thought to be a victim of Munchausen syndrome by proxy, a psychological disorder where a “caregiver feigns, exaggerates or induces illness in (another person) with the primary goal being to get attention, sympathy and praise,” Dr. Marc Feldman, board-certified psychiatrist and author of “Dying to be Ill: True Stories of Medical Deception,” said in a previous interview with TODAY.com.
Read on to learn about them.
2017: A letter leads to love

After watching “Mommy Dead and Dearest,” a 2017 HBO documentary about the murder of Blanchard’s mother, Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard,” as well as the abuse Gypsy Rose Blanchard suffered throughout her upbringing, Urker sent a letter to the then-inmate, who was serving a 10-year sentence at a Missouri state prison.
Nicholas Godejohn, Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s ex-boyfriend who carried out the murder of Dee Dee Blanchard, is serving a life sentence without the possibility of parole after first pleading not guilty.

“I wrote him back and pretty soon we just started writing on a weekly basis,” Blanchard recalled in an interview with E! News. “We became fast friends. It was pretty soon after that that we started talking on the phone. We would spend hours on the phone. I talked to him like I had known him my whole life and vice versa.”

Though their budding relationship began platonically, things changed during Urker’s first face-to-face visit with Blanchard at the Chillicothe Correctional Center. That’s when they shared their first kiss, which Blanchard described to E! as “the most wonderful kiss” of her life.
October 2018: Blanchard and Urker get engaged
The pair grew closer in the year following that first meeting, and during an October 2018 prison visit, Urker popped the question.
Blanchard quoted the special moment in her 2024 memoir, “My Time to Stand.”

“‘Gypsy, I know you through and through and I love you for who you are today, for the heart I’ve come to know,’” she wrote of his proposal. “Then Ken motioned his hands over his chest, over his heart, and continued, ‘I want to spend every day waking up next to you, building a life with you, and being the one that you can come to through all the hard times. I want to be that one for you. Will you marry me?’”
She eagerly accepted.
August 2019: They break up a year later
Their engagement was over less than a year after it began — at least for a while.
In August of 2019, Urker broke up with Blanchard.

“There were many adults in his life, presumably much ‘wiser’ than he, who suggested it wasn’t the right time for me to be married,” Blanchard explained in her book. “‘If you love her, you’ll set her free,’ was the common piece of advice he’d hear again and again, sometimes from prominent Hollywood therapists and other media personalities — sometimes from those in my own immediate family. I see now, he believed he was acting in my best interest by sacrificing his own needs and wants.”
The pair reunited later that month, but the reunion didn’t last.
July 2022: She marries another man

Urker wasn’t the only man to reach out to Blanchard during her incarceration. Louisiana teacher Ryan Scott Anderson began corresponding with her sometime after her split from Urker, and things progressed quickly between Anderson and Blanchard.
They married at the Chillicothe Correctional Center on July 21, 2022.
In the Lifetime documentary, “The Prison Confessions of Gypsy Rose Blanchard,” Anderson referred to himself as “the Prince Charming that Gypsy has been waiting for her whole life.”

Blanchard was released from prison in December 2023, after serving eight years of her sentence. She and Anderson separated months later. In an interview with TODAY.com, Anderson said he was “blindsided” by the split.
Spring 2024: Blanchard and Urker reconnect
In the wake of that separation, Blanchard and her former fiancé, Urker, decided to give their relationship another try.

Urker took to Instagram on April 15, 2024, to share photos from an “incredible weekend” they’d spent together. The carousel of images included several smiling pics of the pair, as well as a glimpse of the matching husky dog tattoos they’d recently gotten to commemorate their bond.
July 2024: They’re expecting
Urker and Blanchard celebrated a surprise event in July of 2024 — a baby on the way.

“This was not planned at all. This was completely unexpected, but we’re both very excited to take on this new journey of parenthood,” Blanchard said in a now deleted TikTok, which TODAY.com reported at the time.
December 2024: Divorce and a new arrival
Blanchard and her estranged husband, Anderson, finalized their divorce Dec. 9, 2024.

“My marriage with Ryan taught me a lot about myself,” Blanchard told TODAY.com. “There was something Ryan said in Season 1 (of the Lifetime series ‘Gypsy Rose: Life After Lock Up’), ‘Life is not a fairy tale. It’s going to have its challenges.’ I didn’t understand that at the time. Now, after going through everything, I apply that to my relationship with Ken. We will have bad days, moments where we feel overwhelmed, but to not give up. Don’t just judge the whole relationship on that one day or that one argument.”
Less than three weeks later, on Dec. 28, Blanchard gave birth to a baby girl named Aurora.
Shortly after Aurora’s arrival, the new mom took to social media to announce that she would not be sharing images of their little girl’s face with her followers.

“To everyone asking, No, I will not be posting pictures of Aurora,” she wrote in an Instagram story. “I understand everyone’s excitement and we appreciate the support, but we value the privacy and safety of our daughter.”
March 2025: Appear on a reality show together

On March 10, 2025, a new season of “Gypsy Rose: Life After Lock Up” is set to debut, promising to give the public a closer look at Blanchard’s life since leaving her last relationship and starting a family with Urker.
Blanchard, who spoke to TODAY.com ahead of the premiere, shared what she hoped viewers would take away show.

“I want them to take away that everyone is growing in their life,” she said. “No one is completely finished evolving who they are. That’s what I was doing the whole season — building my character, learning about myself, discovering what I’m all about.”

title: Jasmine Guillory’s ‘Dirty Dancing’-Inspired YA Romance Is Dedicated to Her Teenage Self. Read The First Page
summary: Jasmine Guillory speaks to TODAY.com about her new novel, “It’s Only Dancing,” sharing how it was inspired by her experience as a young ballet dancer.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
Jasmine Guillory has become synonymous with swoon-worthy adult romances. Now, the author is using her talents to craft a love story that younger audiences can relate to.

The bestselling writer behind “The Proposal” and “The Wedding Date,” which is currently being adapted for the screen, is back with her first-ever young adult novel and 10th overall called “It’s Only Dancing,” out Oct. 6.

The opening of the book immediately thrusts the reader into the world of prickly high school student Kat, who is about to enter her senior year. For her last summer of freedom, her parents decide to whisk her and her younger sister to a camp in the Southern California desert.
TODAY.com is exclusively sharing an excerpt from Chapter 1 of the book, which begins with Kat, a former ballet dancer, expressing her frustrations as the family of four travel to the camp.
I turned the page of my book as loudly as possible, but my family didn’t seem to notice.
Guillory tells TODAY.com that she knew this scene was exactly how she wanted to introduce Kat: She’s a “grumpy” teen who is “the introvert in a family of extroverts.”
Despite her protests, Kat arrives and soon meets a handsome dance instructor named Jordan. He could make this a summer to remember, while also helping her rediscover her passion for dance.

“What’s interesting is that I always loved young adult books and sort of have gone back and forth in tapping into that. When I first started writing, before I was ever published, the first book I wrote was young adult,” Guillory says.
She noticed growing up there weren’t many books centered on teenage Black girls and their experiences.
“I think all of us who grew up Black grew up learning how to relate to people who weren’t us because there weren’t a lot of books about us,” she says.
The idea to pen her own Black young adult novel has been resurfacing for years, and “It’s Only Dancing” is dedicated to her younger self.
“To teenage Jasmine: You needed this book so much. You’re going to do great things,” the dedication page reads.
Like Kat, Guillory studied ballet as a child. And like her guarded protagonist, she didn’t always feel accepted in her dance community.

“I still love ballet, and I love going to the ballet. I’m thrilled to see so many Black ballerinas,” she says. “But it is different when you are a Black girl, and your body changes in ways that are often different from the ways that your white classmates’ bodies change.
“I wanted to explore that and see how Kat was doing a few years after her end with ballet. She pushed it all down and is trying to pretend (it’s) no big deal,” she adds.
Guillory’s YA debut aims to welcome a newer, younger audience who might currently relate to Kat’s story and insecurities. She hopes they feel validated when they read the book.

“A lot of people don’t give enough credit to teenagers. I think people think of teenagers as always hysterical, always making a big deal out of nothing,” she explains. “I think one thing that I want to tell teenagers is the thing that matters to you right now, it does really matter.”

In “It’s Only Dancing” Kat’s parents are understanding and compassionate about the teen’s personal struggles even though they don’t know why their daughter stopped dancing. It’s a different dynamic than the ones portrayed in some of Guillory’s favorite romantic dance films, like “Center Stage” and “Dirty Dancing,” which partly inspired the themes in her new book.

“I wanted to hit the most important, to me, beats of ‘Dirty Dancing.’ Which were the main character coming out of her shell a little bit (and) recognizing that there’s a whole world out there that isn’t just the world that she’s been in,” the author says. “The adults in her life aren’t always right about everything. I wanted (Kat) to have that experience of learning something new and feeling like, ‘Oh wait, I can do this!’”

When readers turn the final page, they should feel like Kat has grown since the moment they met her on her family car ride to the camp, she says. Guillory also teases a triumphant conclusion to Kat’s story similar to the feeling at the end of “Dirty Dancing.”
“That’s what I was really working towards,” she says. “But (how) we get there is different,” she notes.
See how Kat’s journey begins, below.
Read an Excerpt from Jasmine Guillory’s ‘It’s Only Dancing’

I turned the page of my book as loudly as possible, but my family didn’t seem to notice. Yes, whatever, there wasn’t a particularly loud way to turn a page, but couldn’t my parents and my sister see that I was trying to concentrate? Apparently not, because they kept doing their stupid sing-along.
Oh God. Mom put on Madonna.
“Come on, Kitty, sing with us!” Dad said from the driver’s seat as we sped south down Highway Five.
“Stop calling me Kitty! How many times do I have to tell you, my name is Katherine!” If this was what the next month was going to be like, I was going to lose it.
Obviously this was what the next month was going to be like; I already knew it.

My parents had sprung this stupid month long “family camp” on my sister and me; we had both tried to get out of it, but nothing either of us said made a difference. I even used that tried and true excuse that always worked for all high-achieving, type-A parents: But I need to get a lot done on my college applications before school starts in the fall! But that didn’t even work, which was truly out of character for my parents. They usually got so involved in everything Ella and I did (which was its own nightmare) and were sooo excited about me going to college next year. They’d both gone on and on so much about how they’d loved their college experiences and couldn’t wait for me to have my own and the lifelong friends they’d made and blah blah that it had made me want to die, so I was sure bringing up my applications would work. But they’d just said something stupid about how I needed one more summer of freedom and family togetherness before it was time to go away.

title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Just Killed Off One Of The Most Beloved Day 1 Characters. And Fans Are Not OK.
summary: Who died on Ted Lasso? Here’s what happened to Mae in Season 4, Episode 9.
story: WARNING: “Ted Lasso” Season 4, Episode 9 spoilers ahead.
“Ted Lasso” fans are mourning the loss of one of the show’s most beloved characters.

The fourth season of the feel-good sports comedy just aired its penultimate episode — but not without breaking the hearts of fans with the death of Mae Green, the matronly yet straight-shooting bar owner whose honesty has charmed fans since the start of the show.
Her final scenes, however, packed a punch. And, as many fans have pointed out, it’s a fitting way for the character to conclude the arc of the beloved owner of the Crown and Anchor.

“Growing up, all I wanted to do was be a footballer, but women weren’t allowed to play,” Mae, played by Annette Badland, says during a particularly moving scene in which she gives the Lady Greyhounds the pep talk of a lifetime. “You’re talented. You belong on that pitch. I love to see it. So go out there and make an old lady happy. And beat the f--king s--t out of them!”

The episode, entitled “Mae Rides the Bus,” takes place amid a season that follows coach Ted Lasso, played by creator Jason Sudeikis, as he returns to the UK to lead AFC Richmond women’s soccer team, the Lady Greyhounds. In it, Mae gets the golden invite to ride with the team to their match against Bristol City, so that she doesn’t have to make the hours-long journey alone.
“We’re going to roll out the red and blue carpet, give you a little peek behind the curtain and show you how the sausage is made,” Ted tells Mae.

When the Lady Greyhounds arrive at the visiting team locker room, Mae is invited to say a few words before the match. And she delivers. She even leads the huddle before the players run out onto the field.
As the game kicks off, it’s revealed that Mae chooses to join the other fans in the pit, giving up her luxury seat near team owner Rebecca Welton, played by Hannah Waddingham.

While they get off to a rough start, the Lady Greyhounds get going as star striker Gemma Jay, played by Abbie Hern, returns to the pitch after a long knee injury and scores a penalty kick. The second half of the match is all fire and as the team works to clinch the win, Mae can be seen celebrating with the rest of the die-hards.
Things take a turn after the win as a stadium steward is seen tending to someone in the fan pit. Soon, Rebecca is notified by an attendant that “there’s been an incident.”
As the team celebrates in the locker room, Rebecca quietly grabs Ted to break the difficult news. The episode ends with Ted, bowing his head solemnly.

Mae has been an indelible part of the comedy series across its four seasons, often acting as a comforting yet direct voice amid the chaos and shenanigans around AFC Richmond. Her passing has left many fans inconsolable.
One social media user on platform threads described Mae as the “heartbeat of this fan base for the entire series.”
“And this episode reminded us of that before ripping her away,” the Threads user said.
Another fan wrote that Mae’s death was another example of how the show “finds a way to reach straight into my chest and break my heart while somehow healing it.”
The death wasn’t just difficult for fans. Badland told TV Insider that she herself has yet to watch the episode.

“I haven’t seen it,” she told the outlet. “I don’t watch my own work very much anyway, and it’s far too fresh. Maybe in a year or so I’ll peek from behind my hand and have a look, but it’s far too new for me.”
Badland added, however, that after getting love from her Lady Greyhounds in the locker room and spending the day cheering on her team, Mae went out in the best possible way.
“Her last day was probably her best,” Badland said. “She was certainly very, very happy.”
Even the manner in which her death was announced to Ted, Badland explained, was the perfect way to illustrate the circle of life.

“That’s what happens: People are dying or being born, and the rest of life is going on. And you’re incidental, and it’s not a medical drama (where) they suddenly turned up in an ambulance and started pumping my chest, or whatever,” she told the outlet. “I think it’s much more elegant to leave her in that very happy place, in that very fulfilled moment.”
Cheers to you, Mae. The Crown and Anchor will never be the same.

title: ‘Verity’ Ending Explained: Is the Manuscript or Letter Telling the Truth?
summary: Who is the real villain in “Verity”? Here’s what author Colleen Hoover says about the latest big-screen thriller starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Harnett.
story: Warning: This contains spoilers for the movie “Verity.”
If you’ve read Colleen Hoover’s “Verity,” consider yourself primed for the movie adaptation of the psychological thriller.

Released in 2018, Hoover’s dark love triangle shot to the top of the bestseller lists and has since become a cultural phenomenon with readers trying to guess exactly whose version of events is real, and who’s a calculating murderer.

Now Hoover’s twisted love story comes to the big screen. Directed by Michael Showalter, the new film stars Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett as a trio intertwined  in a web of seduction, lies and murder.

If you’ve just seen the movie and are left with more questions than answers – especially its whodunnit-ending – read on to find the clues you need in order to decide for yourself: “Team Manuscript” or “Team Letter.”
What Is ‘Verity’ About?

In the vein of “Basic Instinct” and “Jagged Edge,” the chilling movie centers on Lowen Ashleigh (Johnson), a struggling writer who agrees to finish penning a series of best-selling novels after their famous author, Verity Crawford (Hathaway), suffers an accident.
To do the job, Lowen must first visit Verity’s remote Vermont home, where she discovers Verity in a catatonic state after crashing her car into a tree.
While going through the author’s notes, Lowen finds a hidden manuscript; Verity’s seeming confession of deception and, far worse, the cold-blooded murder of her young daughter, Harper.

Complicating matters is Lowen’s growing attraction to Verity’s husband, Jeremy (Hartnett), along with her concerns over the couple’s 5-year-old son, Crew, who insists he’s been chatting with his non-responsive mother.

When Lowen begins encountering a very-much awake Verity, she starts to question everything, including her sanity. It’s not enough, however, to discourage Lowen from inserting herself into Jeremy and Crew’s life and stepping into Verity’s shoes as far more than just a ghostwriter.
How Does ‘Verity’ End?

In a Hitchcock-inspired climax, Lowen tells Jeremy about the manuscript, revealing that Verity is responsible for the drowning death of his beloved daughter. Beyond that, Lowen is convinced Verity isn’t actually brain dead and has been faking it the entire time.

Enraged, Jeremy confronts Verity and discovers she is, indeed, fully recovered from the accident. Blinded by fury, he strangles her as Lowen stands by, complicit, since she believes Verity intentionally drowned her own daughter and is a threat to the life she now desires with Jeremy.
Together they make Verity’s death look like an accident. Pregnant with Jeremy’s baby, Lowen, Jeremy and Crew move away from the cursed Vermont house. But the story isn’t over.

Months later, Lowen returns to the Vermont house one final time. As she walks the empty rooms she finds a loose floorboard with a letter hidden beneath. It’s from Verity who writes that if someone has found it, it means she and Crew are safe from Jeremy.

She continues by writing that after losing her daughter, Harper, in a tragic, accidental drowning, she channeled her grief into a dark exercise called “antagonistic journaling.” Far from a confession, the manuscript she wrote was a way to cope with her unimaginable loss and that it was pure fiction.

The letter reveals that after rifling through her office, Jeremy discovered the manuscript and read it. Believing Verity murdered their daughter, he staged a car accident to kill her. When it was unsuccessful, Verity faked being catatonic until she could take Crew and escape from Jeremy.
With dawning horror, Lowen reads the letter, realizing she might have colluded in the murder of an innocent woman. More than that, Jeremy, her new love, might have been the one lying all along.
Even so, she says nothing and they drive away, leaving the house and all its dark secrets behind forever.
Which Is Real: The Manuscript or the Letter?
If you’re unsure who’s telling the truth in “Verity,” you’re not alone. Fans have been debating who the real villain is since the book’s release more than eight years ago.

There are plenty of reasons to believe that Verity’s manuscript is legit since there are so many consistencies between what she’s written and the real-life events including the drowning, the teeth marks on the headboard, the red dress and other specific details.
And, if the manuscript is real, Verity would have no problem penning a letter that seemingly proved her innocence and leaving it for Lowen to find.

That said, it’s important to note that Verity is a writer who writes novels from the villain’s point of view. Did she go to a dark place after the death of her daughter and use her writing to deal with the loss? In his own grief and rage, did Jeremy refuse to listen to her explanation of the manuscript and in turn, become a cold-blooded killer?
Beyond that, by the end of the movie it’s clear that Jeremy has been lying to Lowen about any number of things since they day they met, including not knowing who she was, when, in fact, he did.
What Does Colleen Hoover Think?

Perhaps the most helpful hint in solving the mystery is Hoover’s opinion. During a March 2026 appearance on Jenna Bush Hager’s podcast “Open Book with Jenna,” Hoover explained that when she was writing the novel, she was primarily plugged into Lowen’s character.

“I was in Lowen’s head when I wrote it,” Hoover told Jenna. “So, I didn’t really dive into that part of things from Jeremy or Verity’s perspective. So, I walked away from it kind of feeling like Lowen felt – not being really sure. Now, as a reader, I have my opinion.”
And where does Hoover land?
“I’m Team Manuscript.”
Even so, according to the “Verity” author, many endings were considered for the movie before a decision was made on the final conclusion.
“We got a lot of time to test it and edit it,” Hoover tells Jenna. “So, I feel like people will be happy with it.”

title: Pope Leo Sent White Sox A Letter of ‘Abundant Blessings.’ Then They Won Their Playoff Series
summary: Considering how their Wild Card series ended, it appears that the Chicago White Sox truly are #blessed.
story: Considering how their Wild Card series ended, it appears that the Chicago White Sox truly are #blessed.

The team clinched their playoff series Sept. 30 against the Houston Astros after a two-game sweep at Daikin Park in Texas. But as many fans have joked, the historic victory — their first postseason series win in more than two decades — may have been in part due to a bit of divine intervention. It turns out that well-known White Sox fan Pope Leo XIV sent the team a special letter ahead of the high-stakes games.

“I willingly invoke the Almighty’s abundant blessings upon you and your loved ones,” the Pope wrote in the signed letter to White Sox chairman Jerry Reinsdorf that arrived Sept. 29, according to the team’s social media accounts.

The American League Wild Card series win marks the White Sox’ first postseason series victory since they won the World Series in 2005. That championship was coincidentally also against the Astros. And oddly enough, Pope Leo was in the stands for the series opener, rooting his Sox on from Section 140, Row 19, Seat 2.

This time around, the White Sox beat their Texas opponents in just two games for the best-of-three series. The mail that arrived from the Pope, which was dated Sept. 9, referenced a letter that he wrote ahead of the Winter Olympic Games in February.

“As I have noted, ‘sport can truly become a school of life, where all can learn that abundance does not come from victory at any cost, but from sharing, from respecting others and from the joy of walking together,’” he wrote, citing the February letter.

The pope added that it is his “hope that the White Sox will continue to foster bonds of friendship and solidarity among people, and thus bear hopeful witness to the possibility of living and working together in peace.”
Pope Leo’s love of the White Sox is well-documented. In June 2025, he repped his team, stepping out in a Sox cap while meeting newlywed couples at the Vatican.

The South Side team has been more than happy to embrace their famous fan. Earlier in the season, the team gave away White Sox-themed papal miters to fans who attended the team’s Aug. 11 game against the Cincinnati Reds. Weeks later, South Side native Father Tom McCarthy presented the pope with one of the hats as well.
The Chicago White Sox will move on to the American League Division Series, where they will take on the Cleveland Guardians starting Oct. 3.

title: Alix Earle Says the Last Book She Read Was Dr. Seuss. Jenna Has a Reading Syllabus for Her
summary: Alix Earle says she has never read a book, so Jenna Bush Hager is here to help.
story: Alix Earle says she has never read a book, so Jenna Bush Hager is here to help.

The creator of the Read with Jenna book club broke out a reading list for the social media star on TODAY Oct. 1 after Earle, 25, told Interview magazine that she’s “never read a book,” except for “maybe Dr. Seuss.” The revelation sparked backlash and shocked Jenna.
“Alix, you’ve been on the show,” Jenna said on TODAY. “We know that you’re smart, so you know what we want to do, we want to give you a little syllabus.”
Earle reacted to her comment going viral on her Instagram story by reposting a tweet about it, adding the caption, “This is sending me,” per EW.
Before Jenna broke out her reading recommendations for Earle, she and Sheinelle talked about the benefits of curling up wth a book.

“With social media, you have to use your mind quickly,” Jenna said. “When you sit in a book and you’re there for a while it uses a different part of our brain, which is a part that we used a lot back in the day and has been sort of combated with the rise of short videos.
“Reading fiction brings about — and we know this — the rise of empathy,” she continued. “Because you’re sitting in the shoes of somebody else.”
With that said, she offered the following books for Earle.
“Come here, sit on our show, and we can teach you how to be a great reader,” Jenna said.
‘The Baby-Sitter’s Club’
Jenna first recommended the classic children’s book series by Ann M. Martin.
“We know you’re an entrepreneur,” Jenna said. “She started her own brand. This talks about females getting together, starting a club, empowering each other. Let’s start here, Alix.”
‘Are You There God? It’s Me, Margaret’
Judy Blume’s iconic 1970 novel about sixth-grader Margaret Simon has been a rite-of-passage read for generations of kids.
“Alix, if you haven’t learned about sex, this might hit the ticket,” Jenna joked.
‘Of Mice and Men’
The 1937 novella by John Steinbeck about the Depression-era experiences of George Milton and Lennie Small is a staple of scholastic reading lists.
“If you didn’t get assigned this in eighth grade, I want to talk to your English teacher,” Jenna said.
‘Pachinko’
A more contemporary classic, the 2017 novel by Min Jin Lee follows the saga of multiple generations of a Korean family who move to Japan.
“I love this author so much,” Jenna said before showing off the weighty tome. “This is a bigger one, so that’s why you start with these (other books).”
Jenna wasn’t done, and she included a syllabus with seven more books:

title: Leigh Bardugo Reflects on Backlash to ‘Ninth House,’ Her First Novel Written For Adults
summary: Leigh Bardugo looked back at the uproar over content warnings in Ninth House and whether she thinks trigger warnings are necessary.
story: Leigh Bardugo is looking back at a conversation-starting chapter of her career.

The author rose to fame with her sprawling Grishaverse YA novels, set in a magical world. In 2019, she made her adult debut with “Ninth House,” the first book in a trilogy that unfolds among the secret societies of Yale.

At the time of its publication, a graphic assault scene in “Ninth House” sparked a discussion about content warnings. Some readers said they were shocked and disturbed by the scene and that there should have been a warning before reading.
On an episode of Jenna Bush Hager’s “Open Book with Jenna” out Oct. 1, Bardugo said the uproar is “still surprising” to her, “given some of the things that are popular now.”
“There was nothing in this book that really deviated from what you would find in any horror novel or urban fantasy novel, but it was a departure from what I had written for teens,” she said.
Bardugo said while there’s “an argument to be made” for content warnings, she noted that calls for them tend to be loudest for books written by women who previously wrote books for kids.
“I think there’s a very puritanical streak that runs through all this,” she said.
She also said if content warnings are expected, they need to be in every book, “and I’m not interested in being the test case.”

“I believe that things belong on different shelves,” she said. “That where we shelve a book is all about expectations. And if you are coming to a young adult shelf, you would never find ‘Ninth House’ there.”
Bardugo said her first impulse was to be defensive over the backlash to her book’s content. “I didn’t write this for shock value,” she remembered thinking.
Then, she realized the outrage was proof the book was working.

“You should be troubled by this. If you’re reading about an assault on the page. You shouldn’t just be able to skim right past it. It should hit you. It should hit you like a ton of bricks. And if I did that, maybe I did something right,” she said.
Ultimately, she said, the book “found the people it needed to find.” If she had changed or softened its contents, “it would not have found those people.”
Plus, she said, books are an excellent place to raise difficult and uncomfortable topics, “because you’re safe when you’re doing it.”

“(Books) can lead to conversation. They can lead to difficult thoughts that we have about things we’ve been through, things that we’re going through with other people, things that our friends have been through, that maybe we don’t know how to speak to them about. That kind of connection exists in these places of discomfort,” she says.
The final installment of Bardugo’s “Ninth House” series, called “Dead Beat,” came out Sept. 15, wrapping up Alex Stern’s voyage through the magical portals of Yale University.
