title: Khloé Kardashian Recommends These 3 Episodes If You’re New to Her ‘Wonder Land’ Podcast
summary: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields.
story: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment, Khloé Kardashian shares the episodes you should listen to if you’re new to her “Wonder Land” podcast ahead of its Season 4 premiere.
Khloé Kardashian says the first seasons of her “Khloé in Wonder Land” podcast were “trial and error” when it came to setting the tone for the project.
But as the podcast enters its fourth season, the 42-year-old reality star and entrepreneur is feeling confident and ready to continue quenching her curiosity on a number of topics.

“My mind goes anywhere and everywhere. I do want to learn from these experts and have things that are takeaways, and then I also want to talk to someone about spray tans and makeup,” Kardashian tells TODAY.com with a laugh. “And then I also want to go down some rabbit hole about aliens and the pyramids. I want to go everywhere.”

Her genuine curiosity is what has fueled the upcoming season of “Khloé in Wonder Land.” But first, she wants to kick off Season 4 with a “light and fun” episode with TV personality and “Summer House” alum Paige Desorbo.
“Wonder Land” contains multitudes, whether it’s a chat with a medical professional, her best friend or mom Kris Jenner. Kardashian hopes people “find a connection to one of the episodes.”
One conversation that is extra meaningful is her 2025 sit down with the late Dolly Parton.

“The one that I’ve held deepest in my heart is the one with Dolly Parton, which I feel privileged and blessed that I got to interview her,” she says. “And I believe I was like one of her last podcasts that she’s done. To be with her in Tennessee, what a blessing for me.”
Ahead of the “Khloé in Wonder Land” Season 4 premiere on Sept. 30, Kardashian shares the three episodes she recommends if you’re new to her podcast.
Making Contact with Extraterrestrials ft. Dr. Steven Greer

Kardashian’s sit down with Dr. Steven Greer, a leading expert on UFO disclosure, secret government operations and suppressed technology, aired on March 6, 2025. The two discussed theories on hidden alien technology, potential military cover-ups and more.
“If you’re into aliens and conspiracies, I loved my Dr. Steven Greer episode,” she says. “It was fascinating — and whatever you think, you think. But if you’re into it, great!”
Raising Resilient Kids, Setting Limits & Mom Guilt ft. Dr. Becky
Her June 5, 2025 episode with clinical psychologist Dr. Becky Kennedy was informative for Kardashian. The two unpacked mom guilt, setting boundaries, raising resilient children and more.

“I loved Dr. Becky when it came to kids and all the tips that I got from her for those,” the mom of two says, also adding, “How lucky am I that I sit on a couch, I’m asking them questions, but how many takeaways I get to implement into my life and pass on to other people.”
Kardashian adds that when it comes to guests who are experts, “the ones that actually are changing people and helping them, I feel really honored that I have a platform that can provide that.”
Untold Stories Behind the Kardashians ft. Kris Jenner
There’s one special guest that is always a good time, and that’s Kardashian’s mom, Kris Jenner.
Jenner has been on “Wonder Land” a number of times, delivering inside scoop, going down memory lane and sharing her wisdom with her daughter and listeners.

“I love the ones that I do with my mom. I love the nuggets that she gives you, whether it be motherly or silly or just, like, cutesy or some insight on our family,” Kardashian says. “But then she’ll also drop a few gems that you have to pick up along the way.”
Kardashian loves that Jenner has become everyone’s mother, saying, “Thank God, I love it, and she loves it too. It’s the best.”
New episodes of “Khloé in Wonder Land” will drop every Wednesday on YouTube and audio streaming services.

title: Would Jose Iglesias Ever Return to the MLB? What He Told Craig Melvin
summary: Although MLB player Jose Iglesias may have stepped away from baseball, he isn’t completely ruling out a return to the diamond.
story: Although MLB player Jose Iglesias may have stepped away from baseball, he isn’t completely ruling out a return to the diamond.

During his recent appearance on Craig Melvin’s “Glass Half Full” podcast, Iglesias was asked if he would ever consider playing baseball again if the opportunity arose. Iglesias last played in September 2025 for the Padres but has not formally retired from the league.
“If that phone rings, and it’s not Broadway and it’s MLB, I’ll be there because I feel good,” Iglesias told Craig.
Iglesias, 36, made his MLB debut in 2011 and became a free agent after the 2025 season. He’s most recently pivoted to Broadway, debuting in “Buena Vista Social Club” in August 2026.
While Iglesias said he would play in the MLB, he had one caveat.
“I have to have a personal feeling for the team,” he said. “I’m in that state of my life where (it’s) not just to play, but to play for something.”
He then named the two teams that already meet that: the New York Mets and the San Diego Padres.

Iglesias played for the New York Mets during the team’s 2024 Cinderella season, which culminated in a playoff run to the National League Championship. The Mets lost to the Los Angeles Dodgers, just missing a World Series appearance.

Iglesias was a fan favorite during the 2024 season after releasing the song “OMG” under his stage name Candelita. In addition to serving as his walk-up song, “OMG” became the team’s unofficial anthem that season.
The Mets did not resign Iglesias for the 2025 season, and he signed with the Padres.
Iglesias said both the Mets and Padres “opened the door” for him when he thought his career was ending, “so I have to show loyalty for both of them.”
“Any of those organizations would be a privilege, would be an honor,” he added. “And obviously, I hope it’s the Mets.”
“You just made a lot of people very happy,” Craig said.
He then offered Iglesias the hypothetical choice between another Broadway appearance and playing for the Mets.
“You know what? That will be an easy answer,”  Iglesias said. “New York Mets all day long.”

title: Flydubai pilot attacked captain with cockpit’s crash ax in attempted terrorist act, UAE official says
summary: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.
story: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.

The suspect is Omani citizen Hamam al-Hammami, multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East told NBC News. Authorities have not officially released the identity.
The Wall Street Journal, citing sources familiar with the matter, reported that al-Hammami had “previously been banned from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views.”
Oman Air did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether he previously worked for the company.

Emirati officials are leading investigations into the midair incident, which occurred Wednesday on a flight carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A crash was averted, according to eyewitnesses and Israeli officials, when crew and passengers were able to enter the cabin and subdue the attacker.

“Investigations into the incident aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073 revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act,” UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said in an update on Saturday.
“The co-pilot began executing his plan during the flight, attacking the captain inside the flight deck using a crash axe and attempting to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls,” he said.
Al-Hammami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to Abu Dhabi on Thursday, the Saudi Interior Ministry said. The statement said his health had “improved,” but his medical condition was unclear.
Al Shamsi said investigations were ongoing to “establish the full circumstances, motives, and any links related to the incident.”

Israeli government spokesman David Mencer said Friday that Israeli investigators would “join their Emirati counterparts in investigating this attempted mass murder and establishing precisely what happened, his motives and background.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday: “As time passes, the picture becomes clearer: The attacker had undergone Islamist radicalization. He came to crash the plane, along with its passengers.”
He did not say how he reached that conclusion, but added: “We are investigating whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price.”
Netanyahu’s spokesman Doron Spielman told NBC News that the suspect “talks on his social media about killing Jews.”
The flight captain, Indian national Capt. Smit Machchhar, spoke for the first time Friday from a hospital in Abu Dhabi.
Flydubai pilot speaks out follow mid-air attack
Machchhar was widely praised for his efforts to prevent the plane from crashing by opening the cockpit door and allowing passengers and crew members to rush in.
Speaking from his hospital bed, Machchhar said he had been “severely injured” and “could sense that the aircraft was going down.”

“I was acting for my own life, but at the same time, I knew I couldn’t let all of them die,” he said on a video call released by India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, adding that he told himself to “give just one last push” to the cockpit door.
The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi called Machchhar the “Indian braveheart,” saying in an X post Saturday that he “remains under excellent medical care & is recovering well.”

The deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, Hamdan bin Mohammed, posted photos on X after visiting Machchhar in the hospital in which he’s seen kissing the pilot’s head and shaking his hand. Machchhar, with one arm in a cast and medical dressings on his head, appears awake and smiling.
“From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise,” he wrote.
Ayelet Epstein, a 47-year-old Israeli, told NBC News that her 14-year-old daughter asked if they were going to die when they heard shouting and “a huge fall started.”
“I told her, no, I don’t think so, we’re going to be OK,” she said, adding that “I was trying to rationalize things in a hopeful way for her.”
Epstein thanked Machchhar “from the bottom of my heart” for saving their lives, lauding his bravery.

A Flydubai spokesperson said Saturday: “We recognise that there are many questions at this stage; however, the circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation. We are therefore not in a position to comment further beyond our published statements.”
“We remain fully committed to supporting the ongoing investigation and are in close coordination with the relevant government authorities and regulators,” the spokesperson added.
President Donald Trump told reporters Thursday that there would be renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack.
“You just ask them,” he said. “They know what happened. They’ll be hit very hard.”
There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News.
Raf Sanchez and Shira Pinson reported from Tel Aviv. Freddie Clayton reported from London. Tom Winter and Jonathan Dienst reported from New York.

title: U.S. pressures European allies to release diesel reserves as Trump considers export ban
summary: The Trump administration asked European allies to release diesel from their emergency stockpiles to increase global supplies and tamp down on soaring prices.
story: The Trump administration ramped up a pressure campaign Thursday to persuade European allies to release diesel from national emergency stockpiles. The White House says additional diesel from Europe would increase global supplies and potentially keep a lid on soaring prices.
The average U.S. price of diesel has soared by 70% since the war with Iran began, hitting $6.38 per gallon Thursday, according to AAA.
Less than five weeks before the U.S. midterm elections, Republicans are eager for any way to lower domestic fuel prices.

“Our European partners should accelerate delivery on their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions” to energy markets, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Thursday on X.  “American farmers, truckers, and businesses should not be left carrying the burden of a global diesel shortage.”
Shortly after Bessent’s post, Trump told reporters “we may” request that Europe release some of its emergency reserves.
Earlier this week, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright had appeared confident that Europe would agree to tap its reserves.

“You will hear announcements from our friends in Europe about new diesel supplies that’ll come to the market that’ll meaningfully push diesel prices down,” Wright told reporters Wednesday at an event with Trump in the Oval Office.
But as of Thursday evening, those announcements hadn’t materialized.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said he raised the diesel issue at a G20 trade ministers meeting in Milwaukee this week. But he did not suggest that Washington had gotten any firm commitments about emergency reserves.
“We’d love to have a collaborative response” to the global diesel crunch, he told Bloomberg News on Thursday.
Also in Milwaukee were trade ministers from China, India, the United Kingdom and other countries that have been affected by strained global diesel supplies.
So far, however, the message coming from Europe on diesel reserves is a noncommittal one.
The E.U. is “in very close contact with our member states on this ongoing issue,” European Commission energy spokesperson Anna-Kaisa Itkonen told reporters at a media briefing in Brussels.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“We are also having high-level contacts ongoing with the U.S. administration,” she said.

The majority of Europe’s emergency diesel reserves are stored in Germany and France. Both American and European oil refineries have been running at near full capacity for months, churning out as much diesel fuel as possible.

While the Iran war is responsible for the lion’s share of price increases in crude oil and unleaded gasoline around the world, the price of diesel has been outpacing both of them since July, albeit for a different reason.
Russia has traditionally been a major exporter of diesel, but that stopped this summer after Ukrainian drone strikes destroyed Russian refineries.
On July 8, Russia banned the export of diesel in order to preserve its domestic supply. On Wednesday, the Kremlin extended that ban until the end of October.

“We’re tight on diesel because we’ve lost diesel exports from Russia,” Wright said at the White House. “We’ve lost diesel, some diesel exports from the Middle East, although we’re restoring those. And we’ve lost diesel exports from China.”
“That’s a lot of interruptions,” he said.

But whether Europe will tap its emergency reserves of diesel to increase global supply is complicated by the fact that the Trump administration is actively considering a move that is effectively the opposite of what it is asking Europe to do.
On Wednesday, the president mused about imposing a ban on exports of U.S. diesel.
“I’m thinking about it,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. “I speak to Chris and Doug about it a lot,” he said, referring to Wright and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum.
“They sort of think ... it’ll help diesel, but it might raise the price of other things,” he said.
An export ban on U.S. diesel would hit European countries particularly hard.
It would also land at a moment when average U.S. prices for unleaded gas remain almost 50% higher than they were on Feb. 28, the day the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran.

title: U.S. ends ISIS-fighting mission in Iraq as regional security fears mount
summary: Kurdish officials are worried the Biden-era decision was being carried out after Iranian missiles pummeled them this year.
story: The last American troops assigned to fight ISIS in Iraq pulled out of the country Wednesday, ending the mission that dismantled the extremists’ self-declared caliphate but raising fears about what might fill the vacuum as the Iran war grinds on.

Though the Iraqi government welcomed the end of Operation Inherent Resolve, Kurdish officials in the north of the country said they were concerned the Biden-era decision was being carried out even after Iranian missiles pummeled them following the war launched by the United States and Israel earlier this year.

Iran-backed militias in Iraq have attacked U.S. personnel and diplomats, as well as regional allies such as Saudi Arabia. And there are fears Tehran could seek to capitalize on the U.S. withdrawal, with its proxies already celebrating the move, coupled with concerns about a potential resurgence in attacks by the remnants of the Islamic State terrorist group itself.

“We came to fight a caliphate, and there is no longer a caliphate, so we are going home,” President Donald Trump said at the White House on Wednesday, adding that the moment was a “victory for the United States,” as well as a “decisive victory over ISIS, which has been completely decimated, which is the reason we went in there in the first place.”

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the “orderly departure” marked “the successful conclusion of the military mission that defeated ISIS in Iraq,” in a statement Wednesday. “This milestone reflects the success of a 12-year campaign that defeated ISIS as an organized military threat in Iraq and across the region.”

The 2014 U.S.-led mission was successful in dismantling the “caliphate” ISIS governed across around 40% of Iraq and one-third of Syria, sweeping through that territory amid instability that followed the U.S. invasion and subsequent withdrawal.
But ISIS has not been defeated entirely in Iraq.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The group comprises “hundreds of fighters” across seven provincial units, according to a United Nations monitoring report in August. This “limited presence” in desert areas generates $500,000 annually through extortion of farmers and shepherds, the report said. But it is “unable to conduct significant attacks” and is only capable of “unsophisticated operations” following the killing and arrest of leaders, it said.

The U.S. expects Iraqi and Kurdish forces to now “lead the continuing effort to secure Iraq and keep ISIS remnants suppressed,” Parnell’s statement said. The Pentagon will “continue to provide targeted training and intelligence support to our Iraqi partners.”
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who has been lavished with praise by Trump since entering office in July, described the withdrawal as the beginning of “a new phase.”

At a handover ceremony in Baghdad, he said this would be “defined by Iraq’s sovereignty, the strength of its institutions, the readiness of its forces, the unity of its decision-making and balanced partnerships with its friends.”

However, Kurdish officials, who govern the north of Iraq, expressed alarm at the move. The Kurdish Peshmerga Affairs Ministry, which oversees defense, said Monday that the U.S. leaving without establishing any other air defense was “deeply concerning.”
The withdrawal was agreed to under President Joe Biden’s administration in 2024, long before the Iran war drastically changed the region’s security landscape.

The Peshmerga Ministry said Monday that 1,000 ballistic missiles have been fired at its territory by Iran since late February. “Some have hit civilian areas, inflicting injuries, material damage and deaths,” it said, nevertheless expressing “sincere gratitude” to the U.S. and its partners “for their cooperation and support.”

The 2003 U.S.-led invasion saw around 150,000 American troops enter the country, toppling leader Saddam Hussein but also triggering a disastrous sectarian war. That combat operation came to an end in 2011, with almost all of the American personnel withdrawn.

The U.S. returned to fight ISIS in 2014, with personnel numbers peaking at almost 9,000 as of 2017. That operation wound down in 2024, and until this week only a small contingent of around 1,500 remained in the Kurdish-governed north.
After this week, a smaller contingent of U.S. forces will stay in Iraq to protect American diplomats.

Iran-backed militant groups have already celebrated the milestone as “a ​historic victory,” as put by Abu Mojtaba al-Yasiri, a commander in the powerful umbrella group the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, who described it as “a crushing defeat for the American project.”

And though depleted, ISIS itself “is seeking to send a message that the group is still powerful and capable of launching bloody attacks,” according to Col. Khalid al-Bayati, a senior security official in the strategic oil town of Kirkuk.

title: Two Iranian nationals charged over alleged terrorism plot targeting Jewish community in England
summary: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
story: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were charged with “engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts” on or before September 20, according to a British police statement.
The two men had allegedly been in contact with an overseas third-party who might be in Iran in relation to the plot, the Metropolitan Police said.
Salehi and Ahmadyan had components for manufacturing an improvised explosive device and conducted reconnaissance for potential targets, according to the statement.

On Monday, police arrested five British nationals in connection with a massive security operation near a base used by the U.S. Air Force to facilitate strikes on Iran, the counterterrorism officials running the operation said.

The five men, all from London and in their early to mid-20s, were arrested Sunday on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses after three suspicious vehicles were seen moving toward RAF Fairford, a Royal Air Force station about 90 minutes west of London.
The men were released on bail, but police arrested a dual U.K.-Iranian national Thursday in relation to the incident.
For Subscribers
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Wednesday there are strong indications that Tehran played a part in the security incident outside the air base.
For Subscribers
Iran has denied any involvement.
Vicki Evans, the senior national coordinator for counterterrorism policing, said the alleged plot in Manchester was not linked to the incident at the airbase.

“This week also brought into sharp focus some of the wider threats being projected into the UK from Iran,” Evans said in the statement. “While this incident and the investigation into the RAF Fairford incident are not connected in any way, I want to reassure the public that CTP, working with our national security partners, are using the full range of our capabilities to protect the UK from any hostile acts.”

title: Screaming, panicking, blood: Passengers detail horrifying Israel-bound flight
summary: It was too early to say why a pilot stabbed another on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
story: TEL AVIV — A stabbing, an emergency alert, a terrifying midair plunge.
Details are still emerging after an Israel-bound flight carrying 180 people emitted a distress signal Wednesday, raising fears of a possible hijacking when one pilot stabbed the other in the cockpit.
Aviatar Alevi, who was on the Flydubai flight Wednesday, described people “screaming, running, panicking, blood.”
“At the start, I thought it was a plane malfunction, but then I started hearing screaming about the stabbings,” Alevi, 17, told NBC News. “Then I understood the weight of the actual situation.”
“We didn’t know what was going to happen,” he said, adding that the possibility of death “was definitely an option.”
The plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, one of its rudders damaged, apparently by the force of its descent.
The passengers, who had been flying from Dubai, were mobbed by media and flag-waving fellow Israelis after they finally arrived at Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
They said they feared for their lives after the plane plunged more than 14,000 feet in 29 seconds at one point, according to FlightRadar24.
“Imagine sitting on the plane, all scared after you fell down five kilometers. You don’t understand anything,” 16-year-old Peleg Itali told NBC News.

Capt. Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, was recovering in a hospital in Saudi Arabia on Thursday as the other pilot, so far identified only as an Omani citizen, was being interrogated elsewhere in the country. Machchhar was widely praised for his efforts to prevent the plane from crashing, opening the cockpit door and allowing passengers and crewmembers to rush in.

Machchhar and the pilot who initiated the attack were transferred to Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, on Thursday, the Saudi Arabian Interior Ministry said in a statement, citing an unnamed “official source” at the ministry.

“The source indicated that initial investigations conducted by the competent authorities in the Kingdom, with the participation of a security team from the sisterly United Arab Emirates, revealed an assault on the pilot by his co-pilot, resulting in both sustaining various injuries,” the ministry said. “The source confirmed that the pilot and his co-pilot, after their health improved and the medical team cleared them, departed the Kingdom for Abu Dhabi this morning.”
Few details had emerged about the pilot Thursday morning. Questions about a possible motive, including whether it was terrorism-related, hang over the attack.

“I don’t think it was a hijacking. It looks like a suicide attempt, simply because of what this hero, Yaniv, has described,” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on “CBS Evening News” as he praised Yaniv Hayun, who rushed into the cockpit and subdued the attacker.
Hayun, who was pictured with his shirt spattered with blood sitting next to Netanyahu, said he confronted the pilot who initiated the attack, according to the Israeli government press office.
“I grabbed the attacker and choked him, pulled him out first,” Hayun said. “I started pulling the controls.”
“Thank God, we pulled it off. We really put our heads together and worked as a team,” Hayun said, adding: “It was between fear and a sense of a do-or-die situation.”
“We had to win. We had to pull through and come out on top,” he said. Hayun told Netanyahu that he acted based on what he had seen on a TV show and helped stabilize the plane.
Flydubai said on-duty crewmembers on the flight were able to land the plane.
Motive under investigation
Netanyahu said it was still too early to determine why the pilot apparently stabbed his colleague and appeared to try to take over the Flydubai flight and whether Iran was involved.

“We’ve had signs that Iran, in particular through its proxies, was intending to heighten terrorist attacks against Israel and Israeli nationals abroad,” he said. “But I think it’s too early to say whether there was Iranian collusion here.”
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz branded the incident a “jihadist terrorist attack attempt,” without expanding on how he had reached that conclusion.
President Donald Trump also weighed in, calling it “an incredible story.”
“It seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot,” Trump told reporters.
On Thursday, Trump told reporters at the White House that the pilot who initiated the attack could be linked to Iran.
“I would say the answer, based on what I’m hearing, is yes. But we’re working on it right now,” he said.
Asked whether the pilot could have been radicalized or working with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Trump replied, “Could have been, yeah.”
Trump also told reporters Thursday that there would be renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack.
“Oh, they’ll be hit very hard, don’t worry,” he said.
“You just ask them,” he added. “They know what happened. They’ll be hit very hard.”
All the passengers were Israeli, according to Netanyahu’s office. Four were dual American-Israeli citizens, two U.S. officials told NBC News.

With few details about the suspect or any potential motive surrounding the incident, Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for Netanyahu’s office, said there was a “strong opinion” that the incident was a terrorist attack, “but we can’t be sure until we debrief everybody.”
An investigation by Saudi authorities is ongoing, David Mencer, a spokesperson for the Israeli Prime Minister’s Office, said separately.
A senior U.S. official and a Saudi official who were both briefed on the Israeli investigation said the stabbing increasingly looked like an act of terrorism based on early findings.
The United Arab Emirates’ attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, separately ordered an investigation.

His office said the probe would seek to “gather information and evidence, establish the facts and circumstances of the incident, and determine the underlying motives,” in addition to examining “whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose, or involved any prior planning or direction.”

Hessa Alyahya, spokesperson for the Saudi Embassy in the U.S., said authorities were waiting to determine whether the attack was a dispute between the pilots or whether it was an act sponsored by Iran or the Houthis.
Israel and Saudi Arabia do not have official diplomatic relations.

title: What we know about the cockpit stabbing on Israel-bound flight
summary: What we know about the potential midair disaster aboard the Flydubai flight when a pilot attacked his colleague causing the plane to plunge thousands of feet.
story: Questions remain about how a pilot managed to sneak a weapon aboard a plane and stab his fellow pilot before it plunged thousands of feet in mere seconds. The attacker was thwarted, passengers said, and the plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
“We were so scared. We didn’t know what was going to happen,” Aviatar Alevi, a 17-year-old student, told NBC News on Wednesday after he and the rest of the passengers were flown to Tel Aviv.
Here is what we know about the incident and how close it came to resulting in tragedy.
What did passengers see?
Alevi described a harrowing scene aboard the flight, with people “screaming, running, panicking, blood.”
“At the start, I thought it was a plane malfunction, but then I started hearing screaming about the stabbings,” he said.
“We didn’t know what was going to happen,” he said, adding that the possibility of death “was definitely an option.”
Another passenger, Motti Cohen Or, 70, said that he heard a woman shouting that “someone is stabbing someone in the cockpit” before the aircraft dived “toward the ground.”
Yaniv Hayun was pictured in a bloody T-shirt telling cameras he had been among those to enter the cockpit and subdue the attacking pilot.
At Ben Gurion Airport, after the passengers had returned to Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu thanked Hayun, whom he later identified as a plumber.

Three others helped in the effort to save the plane and those aboard, Hayun told reporters. The group struggled to open the cockpit door. “I grabbed the attacker, and choked him, pulled him out first,” he said. “I started pulling the controls.”
“Thank God, we pulled it off. We really put our heads together and worked as a team,” he said. “It was between fear and a sense of a do-or-die situation.”
“We had to win. We had to pull through and come out on top,” he added.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Who is the hero pilot?
Hailed as a hero, Indian pilot Smit ​Machchhar was credited by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on X for saving “the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals.”

Even though he was bleeding heavily, Machchhar managed to unlock the door to the cockpit, Netanyahu told Fox News, allowing crew members and passengers to subdue his colleague and regain control of the plane.
The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said on X that he was admitted to a hospital in Tabuk, where the plane landed, and was “reported to be in stable condition.”

According to his LinkedIn profile, Machchhar, who was also praised on social media by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, worked with India’s SpiceJet ‌airline for more than 11 years before joining Flydubai. He has logged more than 9,750 flying hours, the profile says.

Machchhar trained as a pilot at Mainland Air in the New Zealand city of Dunedin for 18 months, beginning in 2008, the school’s CEO, Philip Kean, told the country’s 1News outlet. Machchhar “did very well” as a student and later returned to India where he worked as a recruiter for the school, Kean said.
What about the alleged attacker?
Few details have been released about the alleged attacker, including his name and his condition.
Two senior U.S. law enforcement officials briefed on the incident told NBC News that investigators say the pilot who began stabbing the other pilot is from Oman.
Omani authorities have not commented, and the Omani Foreign Ministry and the embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment from NBC News.
Netanyahu said the pilot was being investigated in Saudi Arabia, where he was detained after the flight landed.

Both Machchhar and the pilot who initiated the attack were transferred to Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, on Thursday, according to a statement from the Saudi Arabian Interior Ministry, citing an unnamed “official source” at the ministry.

“The source confirmed that the pilot and his co-pilot, after their health improved and the medical team cleared them, departed the Kingdom for Abu Dhabi this morning,” the ministry said in the statement.
Was it an attack?

Based on the early results of the investigation, it increasingly looks like this was an act of terrorism, a senior American official and a Saudi Arabian official briefed on the investigation told NBC News.
Saudi Arabia confirmed an altercation between Machchhar and the co-pilot in the Interior Ministry statement posted Thursday.

“The source indicated that initial investigations conducted by the competent authorities in the Kingdom, with the participation of a security team from the sisterly United Arab Emirates, revealed an assault on the pilot by his co-pilot, resulting in both sustaining various injuries,” the ministry said in the statement.

The United Arab Emirates, which owns Flydubai, is also trying to determine “whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or ‌purpose, or involved prior planning or direction,” the country’s state news agency reported Thursday.
Without providing any evidence, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Wednesday ⁠that preliminary information indicated that the pilot whom he described as a terrorist aimed to crash the plane.
Netanyahu described it as “a serious security incident.”
Speaking in the Oval Office on Wednesday, President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu “at length about this event.”
“It seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot,” he said.
Was Iran involved?
There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News.

And there have been no official suggestions from Israel that the Islamic Republic was behind the attack. Two Israeli security officials told The Associated Press that Israel had not identified any Iranian involvement so far.
On Thursday, Trump told reporters at the White House that the pilot who initiated the attack could be linked to Iran.
“I would say the answer, based on what I’m hearing, is yes. But we’re working on it right now,” he said.
Asked whether the pilot could have been radicalized or working with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Trump replied, “Could have been, yeah.”
Trump also told reporters on Thursday that there would be renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack.
Asked if the U.S. would retaliate against Iran if it was involved in the attack, Trump said, “Oh they’ll be hit very hard, don’t worry.”
“You just ask them,” he added. “They know what happened. They’ll be hit very hard.”
Does it alter anything for American flights?
There are “no credible threats” to U.S. airlines, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told a news conference Wednesday.
But he said the U.S. took every incident like this very seriously “and we continue to look at the procedures that we have in place, and continue to make sure the American people are safe.”
What questions remain?
Aside from his nationality, little is known about the pilot who carried out the attack or his motives for doing so.
Pilots undergo rigorous screening, and it is standard for airlines to vet their backgrounds and check their criminal and employment histories.

They also pass through metal detectors and checkpoints at airports, so it is unclear how he sneaked a weapon aboard the plane. Netanyahu said in his interview with Fox News that Machchhar had apparently been stabbed or hit with ⁠an ax.
It also remains unclear whether air marshals were on board the flight at the time of the incident.

Saudi Arabia has warned that it is too early to draw definitive conclusions about who was responsible for the incident, and Israel and the UAE have announced investigations into what exactly happened on Flydubai Flight 1073.

title: Britain believes Iran was involved in incident near air base used by U.S., prime minister says
summary: Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorist offenses in the incident outside RAF Fairford. Iran had denied any involvement.
story: LONDON — There are strong indications Tehran played a part in a security incident outside a British air base that U.S. forces use to facilitate strikes on Iran, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Wednesday.

Burnham said he had chaired an emergency security meeting this week after the incident, which happened early Sunday. Five men, all British nationals, were arrested on suspicion of terrorist and explosives offenses and were released on bail this week.
“We have been waiting to confirm what we could say, but we can now confirm our belief that Iran played a part,” he said in an interview with Sky News.
“This remains, though, a complex and very serious police investigation, so I can’t say any more at this stage,” he added.
The British Parliament is in recess, but Burnham said he “wouldn’t hesitate” to recall lawmakers “should that be necessary.”
Iran has denied any involvement in the incident.

“The embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in London categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Iran to arrest of five suspects in the vicinity of RAF Fairford base,” the Iranian Embassy in Britain said in a statement Monday on X.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday on X that Burnham was wrongly accusing Iran of having played a role in the incident.

“PM Burnham says the UK Government ‘can confirm our belief that we believe Iran to have played a part’ in the RAF Fairford incident,” Araghchi wrote. “I can confirm Iran’s belief that releasing supposed terrorists working for foreign states really says it all. You’re barking up the wrong tree.”

Police on Thursday arrested a dual U.K.-Iranian national on suspicion of plotting a terror attack following a security incident at a U.S.-run military air base in England that British authorities have linked to Tehran.
The 27-year-old man was arrested in London on Thursday, and police have searched two properties in the U.K. capital, Counter Terrorism Policing said in a statement.
President Donald Trump told reporters Wednesday that the U.S. is closely examining the incident.
Asked whether he was planning any response to Iran, Trump replied: “Well, we are. Look, we are studying it right now. We’re studying it. We’re studying it very hard.”
Add to Google
Add to Google

“U.K. did release a number of people that we caught wanting to blow up a base,” Trump added. “We caught them early, and I’m trying to figure out if that’s for real — that they actually did it. Maybe they did it for a reason, but we’re going to know about that this afternoon, so we’ll report on that.”
On Thursday, Trump said he was surprised that the men were released but expressed support for the U.K. investigation.
“I have a lot of respect, however, for Scotland Yard. I think they know what they’re doing, but I was a little bit surprised,” Trump told reporters at the White House.
In an interview with Fox News on Wednesday night, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel had provided intelligence to the U.K. about an attack.
“We gave the Brits the intel that there was going to be an attack and it’s an Iranian-sponsored attack,” Netanyahu said, without providing additional details.
Burnham’s statements were based on intelligence that has been gathered as a result of the investigation, two senior U.S intelligence officials briefed on the matter told NBC News.
Two calls early Sunday U.K. time alerted authorities that the five people could have been up to something inappropriate, according to one official.
One call to police came from one of the five men in the group at about 12:45 a.m., the official said.
British media previously reported that call.
A local farmer called police around 1:30 a.m. local time — a call that police initially cited as the reason for the tip on the group’s activities, the official said.

No charges have been filed against the men, all in their 20s and from London, who were arrested after three vehicles were seen moving toward RAF Fairford, a British air force station about 90 minutes west of London.
Counterterrorism police later took over the case after a major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated, disrupting life in the normally quiet, rural community of the Cotswolds.

title: What we know about the pilot hailed as a hero for averting crash of Israel-bound plane
summary: He is being hailed around the world as a hero for helping stop a passenger plane bound for Israel from plunging into the ground, despite his own severe injuries.
story: He is being hailed around the world as a hero for helping stop a passenger plane bound for Israel from plunging into the ground, despite his own severe injuries.

Images of Capt. Smit Machchhar covered in blood have gone viral after he fought his fellow pilot, who, according to Israeli officials, stabbed him and attempted to nosedive the plane carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

While bleeding profusely, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing other passengers and the Emirati crew to overpower the other pilot and take control of the aircraft. The flight was diverted to an airport in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely.

The Mumbai native’s actions have “shown the world the highest form of courage” and “prevented another 9/11-like attack from happening,” Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Thursday, after speaking with Machchhar’s family. “The whole world is proud of him,” he added.
Machchhar spoke previously of getting the “aviation bug” at 19 while pursuing a management course to grow his family’s textile business.
He worked for years at a low-cost Indian airline before joining Flydubai and had nearly 10,000 hours of flying experience before Wednesday’s incident.

Machchhar is being treated in a hospital in Tabuk city in northwest Saudi Arabia, with his condition described as “stable” on Wednesday by the Indian Embassy in Riyadh. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Fox News he was “very badly wounded.”

Deepak Mittal, India’s ambassador to the United Arab Emirates, said on X he met with Machchhar’s family on Thursday in Dubai and “conveyed full support of the Government of India in ensuring welfare and wellbeing of the Indian Hero.”
Netanyahu called Machchhar “a true hero.”

“Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic midair disaster,” he said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Machchhar’s former employer, the Indian budget carrier SpiceJet, said on X that he flew for the airline for 10 years. According to his LinkedIn profile, Machchhar joined the Emirati low-cost carrier Flydubai in 2022 after flying for SpiceJet since 2011.

On Wednesday, the veteran captain was flying a Boeing 737 Max 8, the newer variant of the 737 plane that Machchhar had nearly 10,000 hours of experience flying, according to his profile and a YouTube podcast interview he gave last year.
“My first aircraft was a Boeing, and it’s always been that aircraft all my life,” he said.
Machchhar said he had flown challenging routes, dodged bad weather and handled medical emergencies in the air before.
His mother was “scared” when he first told her of his plan to become a pilot, he said in the 2025 interview, but his supportive father agreed to cover the steep fees for aviation training.

Between 2008 and 2009, Machchhar trained for 18 months at an aviation college in New Zealand. It was the first time he had been outside India, he said, and he had been on only a “couple of flights” as a passenger before learning to fly.
He “stood out” among those training and did well with his studies, Mainland Air chief executive Philip Kean told New Zealand’s 1News, adding: “We’re all very proud of him here.”
In his early days as a qualified pilot, he took whatever flight routes he was assigned.
“When I started flying ... the only thing I wanted to do then was fly,” Machchhar told the podcast. “I didn’t want to sleep, I didn’t want to go anywhere, and they loved me for it.”
“For a pilot to gain that experience and to refine your skills is what a pilot is,” he added.
But his attitude changed when he got married and started a family, he said.
“Now I would say I try when I get out of the cockpit or the aircraft, I don’t want the other guy to know that I’m a pilot. I don’t want to discuss aviation,” he said.
“Now the kids are there,” he said. “They want to play with you.”
In the interview, Machchhar also spoke about the “rigorous training” that pilots and cabin crew undergo, which includes safety and emergency procedures.
“When we are up there and if something happens, who is going to save you? You’ll be lucky enough to have a doctor on board,” he said.
“They can save your life,” he said, referring to the cabin crew.

title: Pilot stabbed his co-pilot in apparent attempt to crash Israel-bound plane, Netanyahu says
summary: On-duty crewmembers were able to divert and land the aircraft safely at Tabuk Airport, the airline said.
story: TEL AVIV — A pilot stabbed his co-pilot aboard a plane headed to Israel on Wednesday and may have tried to crash the aircraft with 174 people on board, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said.

“I don’t think it was a hijacking. It looks like a suicide attempt, simply because of what this hero, Yaniv, has described,” Netanyahu said on “CBS Evening News,” referring to Yaniv Hayun, a passenger who said he entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker.
The pilot who initiated the attack is an Omani citizen and is being interrogated in Saudi Arabia, Netanyahu said on the CBS program on Wednesday night.
Netanyahu said a motive was being determined, including whether it was an attempt to commit an act of terrorism. He said he expected the suspect pilot would be moved to Dubai soon.
“He’ll be investigated, interrogated and we’ll join the interrogation, and find out what happened there exactly,” Netanyahu said.
President Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that the attack was “an incredible story.”
“I did speak to Bibi Netanyahu at length about this event, and it seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot,” Trump said.
Passengers lived through scenes of terror as the Flydubai flight approaching Tel Aviv shook violently and abruptly plummeted. The flight had originated in Dubai.

“I thought it was a plane malfunction, but then I started hearing screaming about the stabbings,” Aviatar Alevi, a 17-year-old student, told NBC News. “Then I understood the weight of the actual situation.”
Alevi said he thought he was going to die as he felt the plane rapidly descend, with “screaming, people running, panicking, blood.”
Another passenger, Motti Cohen Or, 70, told NBC News that he heard a woman shouting that “someone is stabbing someone in the cockpit” before the aircraft dived “toward the ground.”
Flight data indicates the Boeing 737, flight number FZ 1073, plunged by 14,125 feet in just 29 seconds, according to Flightradar24.

All Flydubai flights to and from Israel have been temporarily suspended as authorities continue their investigation into what occurred on Flight FZ 1073, a spokesperson for the airline said in a statement.
“This temporary suspension will allow the relevant authorities to continue their work and establish all the facts surrounding the incident,” the spokesperson said in the statement.

The midair incident led to a diversion and an emergency landing at Saudi Arabia’s Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport, known as Tabuk Airport. A rescue flight later brought passengers to Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport.

At Ben Gurion, Netanyahu personally thanked a passenger still wearing a bloodied T-shirt, who told cameras he was among those to enter the cockpit and subdue the attacking pilot. Netanyahu’s office named the man as Hayun. Netanyahu later said that Hayun is a plumber in an interview on Fox News.
Hayun told Netanyahu that, as he made his way to the cockpit, the plane took a steep nose dive which knocked him sideways, according to the Israeli government press office.
Three other passengers helped in the effort to save the plane and those aboard, Hayun told reporters at Ben Gurion.
The group struggled to open the cockpit door.
“We managed to get it open, but what made it difficult for us was the pilot himself — he had been stabbed and was on the other side of the door,” he said.
Netanyahu said on the CBS program that when Hayun went in the cockpit he saw the pilot who had initiated the attack trying to crash the plane.
“He wasn’t sitting in the pilot seat, trying to stabilize the plane, he was trying to jam the equipment,” Netanyahu said.
Hayun told Netanyahu that he confronted the pilot who had initiated the attack, according to the Israeli government press office.
“I grabbed the attacker, and choked him, pulled him out first,” Hayun said. “I started pulling the controls.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Hayun told Netanyahu that he took actions based on what he had seen on a TV show and helped stabilize the plane, according to the Israeli government press office.
“Thank God, we pulled it off. We really put our heads together and worked as a team,” Hayun said.
“It was between fear and a sense of a do-or-die situation,” Hayun added. “We had to win. We had to pull through and come out on top.”

Israeli officials also praised the stabbed pilot, identified as Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar, for his actions in opening the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to rush in, secure the cockpit and prevent the plane from crashing.
“He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals,” Netanyahu said on X. “I wish Captain Machchhar a speedy and full recovery. He is a true hero.”
In the interview on Fox News, Netanyahu said that there were 30 children on the plane.
Video from on board appeared to show two people lying on the floor, visibly bloodied as others crowd around them.
Machchhar is in stable condition in a hospital in Saudi Arabia, according to the Indian Embassy in Riyadh.
Four U.S. citizens, who are dual nationals, were on the flight, per two U.S. officials.
Prime minister’s spokesperson Doron Spielman said that “there is a strong opinion” that the incident was a terror attack, “but we can’t be sure until we debrief everybody.”
No country or terror organization has claimed the incident.
Two senior U.S. law enforcement officials briefed on the investigation also told NBC News that investigators say the pilot who began stabbing the co-pilot is from Oman.
The officials did not name that pilot.
The Omani Embassy in the U.S. did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
An investigation by Saudi authorities is ongoing, David Mencer, a spokesperson for the Israeli Prime Minister’s Office, said.

The stabbing increasingly looks like an act of terrorism based on the early results from the investigation, according to a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation and a Saudi official briefed on the investigation.

The spokesperson for the Saudi Embassy in the U.S., Hessa Alyahya, said authorities were waiting to determine whether the attack was a dispute between the pilots or whether it was an act sponsored by Iran or the Houthis. She said it was expected that more would be known within 24 hours.

Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, deputy prime minister and foreign affairs minister of the United Arab Emirates, and Israel’s foreign affairs minister, Gideon Saar, spoke on the phone Wednesday afternoon.

According to the UAE Foreign Affairs Ministry, Al Nahyan asked about the safety of passengers on the Flydubai flight, which had “experienced a security incident that was successfully brought under control” and wished “good health and well-being” for the passengers.
There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in today’s attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News.
The preliminary Israeli investigation strongly suggests that the incident was an attempted terrorist attack by the Omani pilot who stabbed his co-pilot, the official said.
Netanyahu said on CBS that it was too early to tell if there was any Iranian involvement.

“We’ve had signs that Iran, in particular through its proxies, was intending to heighten terrorist attacks against Israel and Israeli nationals abroad,” Netanyahu said. “But I think it’s too early to say whether there was Iranian collusion here. I think we’ll find out. It won’t take a long time.”
The aircraft was “successfully secured” and landed by on-duty crew traveling on board, Flydubai said.

“At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation,” the airline said, adding: “We urge all parties to refrain from premature speculation while authorities gather the facts.”
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz meanwhile told Israeli media the incident “was a jihadist terrorist attack attempt,” without saying how he reached that conclusion.

After hours on the ground in Saudi Arabia, the diverted passengers were brought back to Ben Gurion Airport, where they were greeted by well-wishers waving Israeli flags and reunited with family members.
Some of those returning waved to the cameras and discussed their experiences, while exhausted parents carried their young children through the terminal.
Peleg Itali, 17, said there was a family with small children near him on the flight.
“The mother doesn’t even know what to tell them,” he said. “No one knows everything, because no one knew what was going on.”

At least one person, a passenger in his 50s, was taken to a hospital with a “chest injury,” said Aryeh Myers, a paramedic with Magen David Adom, Israel’s national emergency agency. Myers described the person’s health condition as “mild.”
Earlier, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee expressed relief on X that the incident didn’t turn out to be “more serious.”
“This had everyone in the Middle East (esp Israel) on FULL ALERT this morning,” he said. “Having pilots inflight detouring to ‘fist city’ not your ordinary experience.”

Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters that domestically, the TSA will continue to be “at high alert,” adding: “We have no credible threats to us right now that would coordinate what took place over there.”

The incident comes at a time of high tensions in Israel ahead of next month’s parliamentary election, a key test for Netanyahu as he faces discontent over Gaza and Iran. The leader has made national security a core part of his platform ahead of the vote on Oct. 27, while also facing pressure from hardliners who favor a more aggressive stance in the West Bank.
Matt Bradley and Yarden Segev reported from Tel Aviv, Chantal Da Silva and Raf Sanchez from London and Nicole Acevedo from New York.

title: British police find no explosives in vehicles of men detained near base used by U.S.
summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the incident near RAF Fairford, which facilitates strikes on Iran, “clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor,” an allegation British officials haven’t confirmed.
story: No explosives were found in vehicles searched after five men were arrested in connection with a huge security operation near an air base the U.S. Air Force uses to facilitate strikes on Iran, British counterterrorism police confirmed Tuesday.

In an update explaining Monday’s decision to release all five suspects who were arrested on terrorism and explosives charges on bail, Laurence Taylor, Britain’s head of counterterrorism policing, said “a quantity” of gasoline was recovered from three vans near RAF Fairford.

“Those vehicles have been subject to extensive examination, with the support of military assets and forensic experts, and we can confirm that no improvised explosive devices were found,” he said, adding that investigators had searched properties in London.
Taylor said it was an “investigative decision” to release the men on bail, “grounded in experience and careful considerations of policing powers.”
No charges have been filed against the men.
President Donald Trump told reporters Tuesday that he was disappointed about that decision.
“I’m just disappointed that they caught terrorists — they did a good job, and then they sort of let them go,” he said, adding, “How do you give bail to a terrorist?”
Asked if it was a long-standing investigation, Trump replied, “A long standing. Yeah, we were involved in it.”
“They put them out on bail. I assume they have, they have them watched closely. But these were serious people, seriously bad people, and they should not have done that,” he added.

Trump also said he was surprised about the decision to release the men on bail on Monday. “I would have said, ‘Don’t let them have bail,’” Trump said in the Oval Office. “I’m surprised that they released them. I wouldn’t have done that.”

title: Settlers clash with Israeli forces to block Palestinian family’s return home
summary: It is the second time the Tubassi family has suffered at the hands of Jewish settlers in just over a month. On Aug. 28, masked settlers attacked and injured them and an NBC News crew that was interviewing them.
story: TEL AVIV — Dozens of Jewish settlers repulsed an attempt by Israeli security forces to return a Palestinian family to its home in the occupied West Bank before setting fire to its property and car.

The Tubassi family was forced to leave its home in July following a weekslong siege by violent settlers in the West Bank town of Jalud. But after security forces tried to enforce an order by Israel’s High Court of Justice to facilitate the family’s return Monday night, an extended and violent confrontation ensued, Mahmoud Tubassi, 60, said.

“I went through a terrifying experience that I could never have imagined,” he said in a telephone interview Tuesday. “We saw death with our own eyes. Death came very close to us at the hands of the settlers.”

It is the second time that Tubassi and his wife, Aida Ahmed Abdullah, 51, have suffered at the hands of Jewish settlers in just over a month. On Aug. 28, masked settlers attacked and injured them and an NBC News crew that was interviewing them. The crew were injured and Abdullah was beaten unconscious but has since recovered.
Add to Google
Add to Google

Tubassi said their latest ordeal began just before midnight Monday when Abdel Azim Wadi, the mayor of the nearby village of Qusra, which has also faced serious settler violence, told him that Israeli officials would accompany him, his wife and their son Wael Tubassi, 33, to their home in Jalud.
After they were picked up by four Israeli vehicles, they were driven the short distance to their home — two structures that sit in a small walled compound atop a hill, he said.
As the family arrived, settlers started throwing stones at the armed police and military, who responded with tear gas and stun grenades, he said.

“They could shoot rubber bullets, they could fire live bullets in air,” Tubassi said of the Israeli security forces’ response. “They could use force, but they didn’t do anything, unfortunately,” he added.

title: A search for their loved ones’ remains, three months after Venezuela earthquakes
summary: Sleeping in tents in front of collapsed buildings and removing rubble with bare hands, family members and volunteers search the ruins with at least 1,500 people missing.
story: LA GUAIRA, Venezuela — Upon entering the ruins of the Jurel building, one hears two things: the murmur of a few curious passersby gazing at the tomb of memories left by the June 24 earthquakes and the creaking of the rubble.

Three months have passed since two earthquakes in quick succession shook this area of ​​the Venezuelan coast. But the devastation continues to resonate for those who haven’t been able to properly say goodbye to loved ones.

Cristian Verdú, 23, lost his brother, his cousin and his mother that day. The bodies of the latter two remain buried in the building’s rubble. A drone search confirmed their location, along with the bodies of other victims.
The building’s collapse is so severe that his search has become — to say the least — nearly impossible after months of searching.

“I never left her alone while she was alive. Anyone who knew my family knew my mother and knew that no matter what happened, I was always there for my mother,” said Verdú, who survived on June 24 because he was in Naiguatá, a town about 45 minutes from Playa Grande, where the Jurel is located.

The search for Verdú’s family went viral following a video posted by journalist Maryorin Méndez in which Verdú pleaded for help recovering his loved ones’ bodies. Others had been able to retrieve their family members’ remains. Finding himself alone, Verdú set up a tent near the Jurel to oversee the search for his mom.

A Mexican rescue team tried to get her out, but the danger of the building collapsing was too great. The Jurel building had 12 floors. Verdú’s mother was on the eighth floor and ended up on the sixth: Its collapse wasn’t like others in that the lower floors partially withstood the earthquake, but the upper floors collapsed one after another.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
What was revealed were the exposed rooms, bathrooms and halls. A swimming pool sloping toward a precipice warns passersby that a tragedy occurred in the building.
‘Still had a conversation to finish’
Verdú recounted that the Jurel was his family’s vacation home; they lived in Caracas, in the 23 de Enero neighborhood, a popular area in the western part of the city.

On the day of the earthquakes, Verdú went for the first time to the San Juan drumming festival, a coastal tradition honoring St. John the Baptist that is celebrated every June 24. Going to the festival is the reason he’s alive, he explained.

The day before, he was with his family and had spent a lot of time with his mother. “My little brother was in the pool, and I spent the day with her. We talked, and she took some secrets with her because I told her things that day, and we still had a conversation to finish,” he told Noticias Telemundo.

When the earthquake struck and he saw that practically nothing remained of his vacation home, he said he experienced a mental breakdown. “I ran out, screaming, not finding my family alive and then having to report that my cousin and a friend of my brother had also died,” Verdú said, adding that it was a difficult situation because other family members thought he had also died.
He immediately began searching for his family, especially his mother.

On the eve of his birthday, almost two months after the earthquake, Verdú announced on social media that he was ending his search for his mom and cousin. Without resources, there was no other option but to leave.
“I wasn’t feeling well anymore. I was exhausted,” Verdú said, adding that the situation was getting more complicated every day.
Even so, Verdú continues to wait and hope. “The case was closed on social media, but the search hasn’t stopped because there are still people who want to get her out and want to help me,” he said.
If they demolish the building with his mother’s and cousin’s remains still inside, Verdú is prepared to continue searching for her, even if it’s among what remains of the rubble.
“It won’t be easy, but believe me, after they demolish the building, I will go back for my mother,” he said, hoping perhaps he can find some peace.
Verdú said that every night he dreams that his mother wants to tell him something, but she always stops or gets scared.

“Many things were left unfinished. My mother’s birthday was coming up, and we had a trip planned, but life had other plans. Perhaps my mother and my little brother had to take a trip that I couldn’t go on,” he said.
Living in a camp, and waiting
Stories like Verdú’s are repeated throughout La Guaira. At Residencias Caribe, family members and volunteer rescuers continue the search for people.
Residencias Caribe was part of a residential development and consisted of three towers. Two of them remained standing; the other collapsed completely.

At the pool area, which overlooks the towers, residents wait for loved ones’ bodies to be recovered. Rescuers don’t have a precise number, but they estimate that more than 70 people’s remains are still in the complex, even though fewer than that number have been declared missing there. Residents have two theories for the discrepancy: Either some people’s relatives didn’t know they were there or entire families perished, with no one left to claim them.

Lying in a tent, next to a fan that cools the air and keeps the mosquitoes away, is Angie Sojo. She has lived in Residencias Caribe for over 20 years and for the past three months has been searching for her husband, Gustavo Adolfo Riascos Gómez, 51.

Her life collapsed along with her home in a single night, and now she awaits news from the rescuers. Sojo’s husband was on the second floor of Tower B of the residences. After the collapse, his body ended up in the parking lot, and for three months they have been trying to recover it without success. Sojo currently lives in the encampment with other neighbors and rescuers who stay overnight.
“At first we all slept on a mattress, and then they started bringing us tents,” she said.

The story of Residencias Caribe is not so different from that of other buildings in the area: There was no help, no rescuers, no supplies. Little by little, some help arrived, and even then, it wasn’t enough.
At Residencias Caribe, the problem isn’t just the collapse, but also the flooding. The first floors are full of water, and pumps have been needed to lower the water level.

On June 24, Sojo was working in Caracas, about 40 minutes from La Guaira. She said that when she got to the building, she was so disoriented that she just started shouting her husband’s name. She and her 20-year-old daughter have been waiting for news for three months and are happy every time a neighbor’s remains are rescued, but she said her heart breaks thinking about when her turn will come.

“It causes anxiety and joy at the same time because it’s another neighbor who’s leaving. I cling to our love,” Sojo said about her husband, “and if it had been the other way around, he’d be here looking for me, too.”
‘Something I owe her’

Valeria Alcalá has been searching for her mother since the earthquakes struck. Alcalá is 18 years old and will soon start university. But for now, she waits every day for news about the search for her mother.
“I’ve been here since it all happened. This has been a constant struggle because I feel like it’s something I owe her,” she said.
Alcalá lost track of her mother and stepfather on June 24. The last time she saw them was the day before, at the San Juan drumming festival. Alcalá remembers them telling her to behave.
They both died in the collapsed buildings; they were downstairs, having arrived five minutes before the earthquakes. Alcalá’s relatives helped her, but they didn’t know where to begin the search.

Her stepfather’s body was found a month ago. It was one of the hardest moments, she said. “Knowing they’re there is not the same as having the body pulled out and having to say, ‘Yes, it’s him.’ Recognizing the body is difficult,” Alcalá said.
She relied on neighbors who had become rescuers. One of them is named Chelo. He also lost his family in the earthquakes and stayed to continue helping fellow former residents.

Nayibe Geromes is searching for her mother, Leída Josefina Mata Cupido, 64. On June 24, she didn’t know if her mother had managed to escape, so she went to shelters hoping for an answer. There was none. Since then, she has been staying at the residences where her mother lived, waiting for her body to be found.
“I’m certain she’s here because they came in and took things that indicate she was here, like her ID, which I still have, her wallet with all her cards, and her cellphone. She’s here,” Geromes said.

The Residencias Caribe residents have become like family after spending three months searching for their loved ones in the rubble. Their only remaining support comes from volunteer rescuers and family members.
“I want to give her eternal rest and get her back so that we too can move on because life goes on. We have cried a lot,” Geromes said.
The neighbors explained that they no longer feel sadness when they find a body and are happy the person’s remains will get the rest they deserve.

“My mom deserves rest. Angie (Sojo)’s husband, all of us who are here I think deserve to be at peace and go home, because this is a tireless fight,” Geromes said, “but I assure you that we will be here until the very end.”
These rescuers aren’t leaving

Marcel Hernández is one of the volunteer rescuers at Residencias Caribe. He has been pulling bodies from the structures for three months. He was a construction worker by trade, but since June 24, he has done nothing but recover corpses. He recounted that the first bodies he recovered at Residencias Caribe were those of his family: his cousin, his cousin’s wife and their four children.
“We started with a pickax — breaking slab after slab. To this day, I haven’t stopped searching,” Hernández said. He got his family out 17 days later.
Hernández promised fellow resident Chelo that they wouldn’t leave until they found his family, and Chelo promised him the same. They insist they won’t leave until they’ve rescued everyone.

Yessamin Medina, known as “La Topito” (“Little Mole”), is another volunteer rescuer at Residencias Caribe. Medina explained that before the earthquakes, she was afraid of the dark and was claustrophobic, but she overcame that fear there.

“I became a ‘mole’ out of love and empathy, without receiving anything in return, simply out of love for my fellow man. I can’t be at home when they still need help here. I’m here out of love for them,” she said.

Medina is 20 years old and became a “mole” thanks to the foundation she created, Puente de Esperanza (Bridge of Hope), after the earthquakes. The volunteer rescuers have left family, homes and jobs to continue helping.

“We have practically been working here with our hands, but with our hands we have achieved many things,” she said, explaining that the lack of machinery and the disastrous nature of the collapse have made the work extremely difficult.
The anguish of the families is the hardest thing, according to Medina. “At home, I’m talking to myself and trying to figure out how I can get them out faster,” she said.
An earlier version of this article was first published by Noticias Telemundo.

title: Terrorism suspects arrested near British air base used by U.S. are released on bail
summary: The five British nationals were detained after a massive security operation near a base the U.S. uses to facilitate strikes on Iran.
story: LONDON — Police have arrested five British nationals in connection with a massive security operation near a base used by the U.S. Air Force to facilitate strikes on Iran, the counterterrorism officials running the operation said Monday.

The five men, all from London and in their early to mid-20s, were arrested Sunday on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses after three suspicious vehicles were seen moving toward RAF Fairford, a Royal Air Force station about 90 minutes west of London.
Dozens of homes were evacuated in the early morning, and a large emergency presence was seen around the installation, shaking the normally quiet area in rural Cotswolds.

But after “extensive interviews and inquiries,” the head of Counter Terrorism Policing, Laurence Taylor, said Monday that they had been released on bail, adding that “does not mean that the investigation is over.”
“They are subject to stringent conditions on their movement and contact with others,” he added.
